sentences.zh: 王湛

translations.literal: Wang Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan

sentences.zh: 王湛，字處沖，司徒渾之弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhan, style name Chuchong, was the younger brother of Minister of Education Wang Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan, courtesy name Chuchong, was the younger brother of Wang Hun, who served as minister of education.

sentences.zh: 少有識度。

translations.literal: In youth he showed discernment and breadth of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a young man he displayed judgment and poise.

sentences.zh: 身長七尺八寸，龍顙大鼻，少言語。

translations.literal: His height was seven chi eight cun; he had a dragon-like forehead and a large nose; he spoke little.
translations.idiomatic: He stood seven chi eight cun tall, with a prominent forehead and a large nose, and he seldom spoke.

sentences.zh: 初有隱德，人莫能知，兄弟宗族皆以為癡，其父昶獨異焉。

translations.literal: At first he had hidden virtue; people could not perceive it; brothers and kin all took him for a fool; only his father Chang regarded him differently.
translations.idiomatic: He concealed his worth at first, so others failed to see it; brothers and clansmen dismissed him as dull-witted, yet his father Wang Chang alone sensed something singular in him.

sentences.zh: 遭父喪，居於墓次。

translations.literal: When his father died, he dwelt beside the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's death he mourned in a hut beside the grave.

sentences.zh: 服闋，闔門守靜，不交當世，沖素簡淡，器量隤然，有公輔之望。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he kept his gates closed and preserved quiet; he did not associate with the prominent men of the age; he was plain, austere, and spare; his bearing was relaxed and ample; he had the expectation of becoming minister or counsellor.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he shut his doors and lived in seclusion, avoiding contact with contemporary notables. Plain and undemonstrative, he carried himself with unhurried breadth, and observers looked to him as future material for the highest offices.

sentences.zh: 兄子濟輕之，所食方丈盈前，不以及淇。

translations.literal: His elder brother's son Ji slighted him; the food before him filled a square yard, yet he did not extend [any] to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Wang Ji looked down on him; though dishes covered the table before Ji, he never offered his uncle Wang Zhan a share (the graph in the text suggests Qi but means Zhan).

sentences.zh: 湛命取菜蔬，對而食之。

translations.literal: Zhan ordered vegetables brought and ate them opposite [Ji].
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan had plain vegetables brought and ate them alongside him.

sentences.zh: 濟嘗詣湛，見床頭有《周易》，問曰：「叔父何用此為？

translations.literal: Ji once visited Zhan and saw the Zhou yi by the couch-head; he asked, saying, 'Uncle, what use do you have for this?'
translations.idiomatic: Once when Wang Ji called on him, he noticed the Book of Changes by the bed and asked, 'Uncle, why keep this?'

sentences.zh: 」湛曰：「體中不佳時，脫復看耳。

translations.literal: Zhan said, 'When my body is not well, I merely look at it again [for diversion].'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan replied, 'When I feel poorly, I leaf through it—that is all.'

sentences.zh: 」濟請言之。

translations.literal: Ji requested that [Zhan] speak on it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji pressed him to elaborate.

sentences.zh: 湛因剖析玄理，微妙有奇趣，皆濟所未聞也。

translations.literal: Zhan thereupon analysed arcane principles; it was subtle and had marvellous interest—all things Ji had never heard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan then unfolded abstruse doctrines with such subtlety and unexpected insight that Wang Ji had never heard their like.

sentences.zh: 濟才氣抗邁，於湛略無子侄之敬。

translations.literal: Ji's talent and spirit were high-striding; toward Zhan he had almost no respect due from nephew to uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Brash and self-assured, Wang Ji had shown his uncle almost none of the deference expected between nephew and elder.

sentences.zh: 既聞其言，不覺栗然，心形俱肅。

translations.literal: Having heard his words, [Ji] unconsciously became trembling; heart and form alike grew solemn.
translations.idiomatic: After hearing him, Wang Ji was shaken to the core; inwardly and outwardly he came to full reverence.

sentences.zh: 遂留連彌日累夜，自視缺然，乃歎曰：「家有名士，三十年而不知，濟之罪也。

translations.literal: Thereupon [he] lingered many days and successive nights; viewing himself as deficient, he sighed, saying, 'The household had a noted scholar, and for thirty years I did not know—this is Ji's fault.'
translations.idiomatic: He stayed on for days and nights, suddenly feeling how wanting he was, and sighed, 'A true gentleman lived under our roof for thirty years and I never saw it—the fault is mine.'

sentences.zh: 」既而辭去，湛送至門。

translations.literal: Presently [Ji] took leave and departed; Zhan escorted him to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When he finally took his leave, Wang Zhan walked him to the gate.

sentences.zh: 濟有從馬絕難乘，濟問湛曰：「叔頗好騎不？

translations.literal: Ji had a gelding extremely difficult to ride; Ji asked Zhan, saying, 'Uncle, do you rather like riding?'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji owned a notoriously unridden gelding and asked, 'Uncle, do you enjoy riding?'

sentences.zh: 」湛曰：「亦好之。

translations.literal: Zhan said, 'I also like it.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan said, 'I do.'

sentences.zh: 」因騎此馬，姿容既妙，回策如縈，善騎者無以過之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he rode this horse; his posture was already marvellous; turning the crop was like winding silk; skilled riders had nothing by which to surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted the beast; his seat was superb and the reins moved in fluid circles—no accomplished rider could have outdone him.

sentences.zh: 又濟所乘馬，甚愛之，湛曰：「此馬雖快，然力薄不堪苦行。

translations.literal: Further, the horse Ji rode he greatly loved; Zhan said, 'This horse, though fast, yet its strength is thin and cannot endure hard travel.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji was devoted to another mount; Wang Zhan observed, 'That horse is swift but lacks stamina for long hard rides.'

sentences.zh: 近見督郵馬當勝，但芻秣不至耳。

translations.literal: Recently I saw the postal inspector's horse—it ought to be superior; only fodder has not reached [it].'
translations.idiomatic: The courier's horse I saw lately should be the better animal—it simply has not been properly fed.'

sentences.zh: 」濟試養之，而與己馬等。

translations.literal: Ji tried feeding it, and it became equal to his own horse.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji tried feeding it as suggested and found it matched his own horse.

sentences.zh: 湛又曰：「此馬任重方知之，平路無以別也。

translations.literal: Zhan further said, 'This horse—only when bearing heavy burden does one know it; on level road there is no means to distinguish.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan added, 'You only learn what such horses are worth under a heavy load; on flat ground they look the same.'

sentences.zh: 」於是當蟻封內試之，濟馬果躓，而督郵馬如常。

translations.literal: Thereupon within an ant-hill ramp they tested them; Ji's horse indeed stumbled, whereas the postal inspector's horse was as usual.
translations.idiomatic: They raced them up a modest slope: Wang Ji's horse stumbled while the courier's mount kept its footing.

sentences.zh: 濟益歎，還白其父，曰：「濟始得一叔，乃濟以上人也。

translations.literal: Ji increasingly marvelled; returning he informed his father, saying, 'Ji has only now gained one uncle—he is a man above Ji.'
translations.idiomatic: More astonished than ever, Wang Ji told his father, 'I have only now discovered my uncle—he is my superior in every way.'

sentences.zh: 」武帝亦以湛為癡，每見濟，輒調之曰：「卿家癡叔死未？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also took Zhan for a fool; whenever he saw Ji, he would tease him, saying, 'Has your household fool uncle died yet?'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu too thought Wang Zhan simple-minded; whenever he saw Wang Ji he would jest, 'Has that dotard uncle of yours died yet?'

sentences.zh: 」濟常無以答。

translations.literal: Ji constantly had nothing wherewith to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji usually had no reply.

sentences.zh: 及是，帝又問如初，濟曰：「臣叔殊不癡。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor again asked as before; Ji said, 'Your subject's uncle is by no means a fool.'
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor put the same question again, Wang Ji answered, 'My uncle is anything but a fool.'

sentences.zh: 」因稱其美。

translations.literal: Thereupon he praised his excellences.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to praise his qualities.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「誰比？

translations.literal: The emperor said, 'Compared with whom?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, 'Whom would you compare him to?'

sentences.zh: 」濟曰：「山濤以下，魏舒以上。

translations.literal: Ji said, 'Below Shan Tao, above Wei Shu.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ji replied, 'Below Shan Tao, above Wei Shu.'

sentences.zh: 」時人謂湛上方山濤不足，下比魏舒有餘。

translations.literal: Men of the time said [that in speaking of] Zhan's being above Shan Tao [the praise] was insufficient; compared below to Wei Shu there was surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners felt Wang Ji still understated his uncle: Wang Zhan towered above Shan Tao, with ample margin left beyond Wei Shu.

sentences.zh: 湛聞曰：「欲處我于季孟之間乎？」

translations.literal: When Zhan heard, he said, 'Do they wish to place me between Ji and Meng?'
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Wang Zhan remarked, 'So they mean to situate me between the lesser and the greater?'

sentences.zh: 湛少仕歷秦王文學、太子洗馬、尚書郎、太子中庶子，出為汝南內史。

translations.literal: In youth Zhan served in succession as literary scholar to the Prince of Qin, groom of the heir-apparent, gentleman of the masters of writing, and palace attendant to the heir-apparent; he went out as interior minister of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhan's early career took him through tutor to the Prince of Qin, attendant for the heir apparent, secretary in the masters-of-writing office, and palace aide to the heir apparent, before he left the capital as governor of Runan commandery.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: He died, age forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子承嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Cheng inherited his position.

translations.literal: Equals sign (continuity marker in source text).

sentences.zh: 子承

translations.literal: Son Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng (his son)

sentences.zh: =承字安期。

translations.literal: = Cheng's style name was Anqi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng, courtesy name Anqi,

sentences.zh: 清虛寡欲，無所修尚。

translations.literal: Clear and empty, few desires; he cultivated and esteemed nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He was spare in habit and free from craving, pursuing no ostentatious cultivation.

sentences.zh: 言理辯物，但明其指要而不飾文辭，有識者服其約而能通。

translations.literal: In discussing principle and discriminating things, he only clarified their gist and did not adorn literary phrasing; knowledgeable men admired his concision yet ability to penetrate.
translations.idiomatic: When he discussed ideas or analysed affairs he laid bare essentials without rhetorical flourish; discerning listeners admired how much clarity he packed into few words.

sentences.zh: 弱冠知名。

translations.literal: At the capping age he became known.
translations.idiomatic: He was already celebrated when he came of age.

sentences.zh: 太尉王衍雅貴異之，比南陽樂廣焉。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Wang Yan nobly prized him as unusual and compared him to Yue Guang of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Wang Yan esteemed him as exceptional and likened him to Yue Guang of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 永寧初，為驃騎參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongning, he became army adjutant to the general of agile cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongning era he served as military aide to the commander of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 值天下將亂，乃避難南下。

translations.literal: It happened that the realm was about to be in turmoil; thereupon he fled disaster and went south.
translations.idiomatic: As the realm slid toward chaos he moved south to escape the storm.

sentences.zh: 遷司空從事中郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to secretariat adviser to the minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to adviser on the staff of the minister of works.

sentences.zh: 豫迎大駕，賜爵藍田縣侯。

translations.literal: He participated in welcoming the great carriage and was granted noble rank as marquis of Lantian county.
translations.idiomatic: For joining the welcome of the imperial train he received the county marquisate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書郎，不就。

translations.literal: He was transferred to gentleman of the masters of writing; he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered a post as secretary in the masters-of-writing department but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 東海王越鎮許，以為記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of the Eastern Sea, Sima Yue, garrisoned Xu, he appointed [Wang Cheng] secretary-adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima Yue of Donghai held Xu, he named Wang Cheng secretary on his staff.

sentences.zh: 雅相知重，敕其子毗曰：「夫學之所益者淺，體之所安者深。

translations.literal: [Yue] nobly knew and esteemed him; he instructed his son Pi, saying, 'What learning adds is shallow; what embodiment settles is deep.'
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue trusted him deeply and told his son Pi, 'Book learning yields thin profit; what you absorb from a living example runs far deeper.'

sentences.zh: 閑習禮度，不如式瞻儀形；

translations.literal: Leisurely practising ritual norms is not as good as ceremonially gazing at deportment and form.'
translations.idiomatic: Drilling etiquette in the abstract cannot compare with watching a master embody it.'

sentences.zh: 諷味遺言，不若親承音旨。

translations.literal: Chanting and savouring transmitted words is not like personally receiving vocal intention.'
translations.idiomatic: Parsing dead texts is nothing beside hearing the man's voice and intent in person.'

sentences.zh: 王參軍人倫之表，汝其師之。

translations.literal: Adjutant Wang is the surface-mark of human relations—take him as your teacher.'
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Wang models what human excellence looks like—make him your teacher.'

sentences.zh: 」在府數年，見朝政漸替，辭以母老，求出。

translations.literal: Having been in the headquarters several years, seeing court governance gradually decline, he took leave citing his mother's age and sought to go out.
translations.idiomatic: After several years on staff, watching central policy fray, he asked to leave on grounds of his mother's age.

sentences.zh: 越不許。

translations.literal: Yue did not permit.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue refused.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷東海太守，政尚清淨，不為細察。

translations.literal: After a long time he was transferred to governor of Donghai; his governance esteemed clarity and quiet; he did not conduct minute inspections.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he became governor of Donghai, ruling through restraint and avoiding petty scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 小吏有盜池不魚者，綱紀推之，承曰：「文王之囿與眾共之，池魚復何足惜耶！

translations.literal: There was a petty clerk who stole fish from the pond (text defective: 不 for 中); the steward prosecuted him; Cheng said, 'King Wen's park was shared with the multitude—what are pond fish again worth regretting!'
translations.idiomatic: When a clerk stole fish from the pond, his administrators pressed charges; Wang Cheng said, 'King Wen shared his hunting park with the people—why begrudge a few fish?'

sentences.zh: 」有犯夜者，為吏所拘，承問其故，答曰：「從師受書，不覺日暮。

translations.literal: There was one who violated the night curfew; he was seized by clerks; Cheng asked the reason; [the man] answered, saying, 'I followed a teacher receiving books; I did not notice the sun had set.'
translations.idiomatic: When someone broke curfew and was detained, Wang Cheng asked why and heard, 'I was studying with my tutor and lost track of dusk.'

sentences.zh: 」承曰：「鞭撻寧越以立威名，非政化之本。

translations.literal: Cheng said, 'To whip Ning Yue to establish a fearsome name is not the root of governance and transformation.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng answered, 'Flogging a diligent student like Ning Yue merely to strike fear is no foundation for humane rule.'

sentences.zh: 」使吏送，令歸家。

translations.literal: He ordered clerks to escort [him] and let him return home.
translations.idiomatic: He had the clerks escort the man home.

sentences.zh: 其從容寬恕若此。

translations.literal: His composure and forgiveness were like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his unruffled magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 尋去官，東渡江。

translations.literal: Soon he left office and crossed east over the river.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned and crossed the Yangzi eastward.

sentences.zh: 是時道路梗澀，人懷危懼，承每遇艱險，處之夷然，雖家人近習，不見其憂喜之色。

translations.literal: At this time roads were blocked and perilous; men harboured peril and fear; whenever Cheng encountered hardship and danger, he dwelt with it peacefully; though family members and intimate attendants, they did not see the colour of worry or joy on him.
translations.idiomatic: Travel was treacherous and fear widespread, yet whenever hardship arose Wang Cheng remained unruffled—those closest to him never caught pleasure or anxiety on his face.

sentences.zh: 既至下邳，登山北望，歎曰：「人言愁，我始欲愁矣。

translations.literal: Having reached Xiapi, he climbed a mountain and looked north; he sighed, saying, 'Men speak of sorrow—I only now begin to wish to sorrow.'
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Xiapi, he climbed a hill, gazed north, and sighed, 'Others speak of grief—only now do I feel its pull.'

sentences.zh: 」及至建鄴，為元帝鎮東府從事中郎，甚見優禮。

translations.literal: When he arrived at Jianye, he became secretariat adviser to Yuan-di's headquarters of eastern garrison; he was greatly shown excellent courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianye he served as staff adviser to Emperor Yuan's eastern command and received exceptional marks of favour.

sentences.zh: 承少有重譽，而推誠接物，盡弘恕之理，故眾咸親愛焉。

translations.literal: Cheng from youth had heavy reputation; yet he extended sincerity in receiving things and exhausted the principle of magnanimous forgiveness; therefore the multitude all drew close and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Already esteemed in youth, he treated people with open sincerity and generous forbearance, so everyone felt drawn to him.

sentences.zh: 渡江名臣王導、衛玠、周顗、庾亮之徒皆出其下，為中興第一。

translations.literal: Among the noted ministers who crossed the river—Wang Dao, Wei Jie, Zhou Yi, Yu Liang, and their sort—all came out below him; he was first of the restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Even luminaries who had crossed the river—Wang Dao, Wei Jie, Zhou Yi, Yu Liang—ranked behind him; contemporaries judged him foremost among those who rebuilt the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 年四十六卒，朝野痛惜之。

translations.literal: He died at forty-six; court and wild alike painfully regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-six to widespread grief at court and beyond.

sentences.zh: 自昶至承，世有高名，論者以為祖不及孫，孫不及父。

translations.literal: From Chang to Cheng, generations had high reputation; discussants thought the grandfather did not match the grandson, the grandson did not match the father.
translations.idiomatic: From Wang Chang through Wang Cheng each generation enjoyed renown; critics held that the grandfather fell short of the grandson, yet the grandson still did not equal his father.

sentences.zh: 子述嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Shu inherited the title.

translations.literal: Equals sign (continuity marker in source text).

sentences.zh: 承子述

translations.literal: Cheng's son Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu (son of Wang Cheng)

sentences.zh: =述字懷祖。

translations.literal: = Shu's style name was Huaizu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu, courtesy name Huaizu,

sentences.zh: 少孤，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned; serving his mother he was heard of for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he earned a reputation for devotion to his mother.

sentences.zh: 安貧守約，不求聞達。

translations.literal: He dwelt in poverty guarding restraint; he did not seek fame and advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Content with poverty and simple restraint, he sought neither fame nor promotion.

sentences.zh: 性沈靜，每坐客馳辨，異端競起，而述處之恬如也。

translations.literal: By nature he was deep and still; whenever seated guests galloped in disputation and rival doctrines competed to arise, yet Shu dwelt with it tranquilly thus.
translations.idiomatic: By temperament reserved, he remained unruffled when guests argued fiercely and rival doctrines clashed around him.

sentences.zh: 少襲父爵。

translations.literal: In youth he inherited his father's noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: He succeeded to his father's noble title while still young.

sentences.zh: 年三十，尚未知名，人或謂之癡。

translations.literal: At age thirty he had still not become known; some people called him a fool.
translations.idiomatic: At thirty he was still obscure, and some dismissed him as slow-witted.

sentences.zh: 司徒王導以門地辟為中兵屬。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Dao on account of family status summoned him as subordinate of central command.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Dao recruited him for the central military staff on the strength of his lineage.

sentences.zh: 既見，無他言，惟問以江東米價。

translations.literal: Once they met, there was no other speech; only he asked him with regard to east-of-the-Yangzi rice prices.
translations.idiomatic: At their first meeting Wang Dao said nothing else—he merely asked the price of rice east of the river.

sentences.zh: 述但張目不答。

translations.literal: Shu only opened his eyes wide and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu only stared back and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 導曰：「王掾不癡，人何言癡也？

translations.literal: Dao said, 'Adjutant Wang is not a fool—why do people call him a fool?'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao remarked, 'This aide is no fool—why does everyone call him one?'

sentences.zh: 」嘗見導每發言，一坐莫不讚美，述正色曰：「人非堯舜，何得每事盡善！

translations.literal: He once saw that whenever Dao spoke, the whole sitting party none did not praise; Shu with straight demeanour said, 'Men are not Yao and Shun—how can each affair reach complete goodness!'
translations.idiomatic: Once, when every guest praised whatever Wang Dao said, Wang Shu spoke sternly: 'We are not Yao and Shun—no one can be right about everything.'

sentences.zh: 」導改容謝之，庾亮曰：「懷祖清貞簡貴，不減祖、父，但曠淡微不及耳。」

translations.literal: Dao changed countenance and apologized to him; Yu Liang said, 'Huaizu is pure, chaste, spare, and noble—not inferior to grandfather and father; only in broad emptiness he is slightly not equal.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao flushed and apologized. Yu Liang observed, 'Huaizu matches his forebears in integrity and understated dignity—only in expansive ease does he fall a little short.'

sentences.zh: 康帝為驃騎將軍，召補功曹，出為宛陵令。

translations.literal: When Emperor Kang was general of agile cavalry, [Wang Shu] was summoned to supplement merit clerk; he went out as magistrate of Wanling.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Kang held the post of commander of agile cavalry, Wang Shu was called up as merit clerk and later left the capital to serve as magistrate of Wanling.

sentences.zh: 太尉、司空頻辟，又除尚書吏部郎，並不行。

translations.literal: Grand commandant and minister of works repeatedly summoned him; further he was appointed gentleman of the personnel bureau of the masters of writing—and in all cases did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated summons from the grand commandant and minister of works, plus appointment as personnel secretary in the masters-of-writing department, all went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 曆庾冰征虜長史。

translations.literal: He passed through chief clerk to Yu Bing, conqueror of barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as senior clerk to Yu Bing, general who conquered the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 時庾翼鎮武昌，以累有妖怪，又猛獸入府，欲移鎮避之。

translations.literal: At the time Yu Yi garrisoned Wuchang; because repeatedly there were monsters and spirits, further a fierce beast entered the headquarters; he wished to shift the garrison to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi was stationed at Wuchang when repeated apparitions and even a beast inside headquarters convinced him to relocate.

sentences.zh: 述與冰箋曰：

translations.literal: Shu wrote a note to Bing, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu sent Yu Bing a letter:

sentences.zh: 竊聞安西欲移鎮樂鄉，不審此為算邪，將為情邪？

translations.literal: I privately hear the Western Pacifier wishes to shift the garrison to Lexiang; I do not know whether this is calculation or emotion?'
translations.idiomatic: I hear the Western Pacifier plans to relocate to Lexiang—is that sound strategy or mere unease?'

sentences.zh: 若謂為算，則彼去武昌千有餘里，數萬之眾造創移徒，方當興立城壁，公私勞擾。

translations.literal: If we say it is calculation, then that place is more than a thousand li from Wuchang; multitudes of tens of thousands will begin removal and migration; just when they should raise and establish walls, public and private labour and turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: If the move is supposed to be strategic, Lexiang lies over a thousand li from Wuchang; marching tens of thousands there means raising new fortifications and exhausting officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 若信要害之地，所宜進據，猶當計移徙之煩，權二者輕重，況此非今日之要邪！

translations.literal: If we trust it is key terrain that ought to be advanced and occupied, still we ought to calculate the trouble of removal and weigh the two sides' light and heavy—moreover is this not today's necessity!'
translations.idiomatic: Even if the site were critical ground worth seizing, one must weigh the cost of relocation—and in any case this cannot be the urgent priority now!'

sentences.zh: 方今強胡陸梁，當畜力養銳，而無故遷動，自取非算。

translations.literal: Just now the mighty Hu rampage; we ought to store strength and nurture sharpness; yet without cause shifting movement—we invite unsound strategy.'
translations.idiomatic: The northern tribes still swagger; we should husband strength—yet you would stir the army without cause and court a strategic blunder.'

sentences.zh: 又江州當溯流數千，供繼軍府，力役增倍，疲曳道路。

translations.literal: Further Jiangzhou must ascend current several thousand; supplying and continuing the military headquarters—labour service doubles; weary dragging on the roads.'
translations.idiomatic: Supplies for Jiangzhou must come thousands of li upstream, doubling corvée and wearing down every road.'

sentences.zh: 且武昌實是江東鎮戍之中，非但捍禦上流而已。

translations.literal: Moreover Wuchang truly is among the middle of Jiangdong's garrison defences; not only defending the upper flow alone.'
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang sits at the heart of our eastern defenses—it is far more than a shield for the upper river.'

sentences.zh: 急緩赴告，駿奔不難。

translations.literal: Urgent and slack, rushing to report—swift running is not difficult.'
translations.idiomatic: Whether the crisis is sudden or slow, couriers can race there without strain.'

sentences.zh: 若移樂鄉，遠在西陲，一朝江渚有虞，不相接救。

translations.literal: If one shifts to Lexiang, far on the western margin—should the river islets one morning have alarm, they will not join rescue.'
translations.idiomatic: Shift to distant Lexiang on the western rim and, should trouble flare along the midstream islets, no help can arrive in time.'

sentences.zh: 方嶽取重將，故當居要害之地，為內外形勢。

translations.literal: The regional pillar-posts employ weighty commanders; therefore they ought to occupy key terrain, forming inner and outer strategic posture.'
translations.idiomatic: Commanders who anchor the provinces must hold terrain that ties the heartland to the frontier.'

sentences.zh: 使窺窬之心不知所向。

translations.literal: Making hearts of peering and coveting not know whither they turn.'
translations.idiomatic: Only then do hostile designs lose their bearing.'

sentences.zh: 若是情邪，則天道玄遠，鬼神難言，妖祥吉凶，誰知其故！

translations.literal: If this is sentiment, then the Way of Heaven is dark and distant; ghosts and spirits are hard to speak of; omens of calamity and auspiciousness, fortune and ill—who knows their causes!
translations.idiomatic: If the move is mere sentiment, then Heaven's workings are unfathomable, spirits defy explanation, and no one can parse omens of weal or woe—why pretend otherwise?

sentences.zh: 是以達人君子直道而行，不以情失。

translations.literal: Therefore accomplished men and gentlemen walk the straight path and do not lose [their way] through sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment therefore hold to principle instead of indulging private mood.

sentences.zh: 昔秦忌：「亡胡」之讖，卒為劉項之資；

translations.literal: Formerly Qin dreaded the prophecy 'the Hu will perish'; in the end it became capital for Liu and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qin once feared the prophecy that 'the barbarians would destroy Qin,' yet it only armed Liu Bang and Xiang Yu against the throne.

sentences.zh: 周惡檿弧之謠，而成褒姒之亂。

translations.literal: Zhou loathed the mulberry-bow mulberry-arrow song, yet there occurred Baosi's turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou dreaded the folksong about mulberry bows, yet still reaped the disaster of Baosi.

sentences.zh: 此既然矣。

translations.literal: This being already thus.
translations.idiomatic: History has shown this plainly.

sentences.zh: 曆觀古今，鑒其遺事，妖異速禍敗者，蓋不少矣，禳避之道，苟非所審，且當擇人事之勝理，思社稷之長計，斯則天下幸甚，令名可保矣。

translations.literal: Surveying past and present in sequence, mirroring their leftover affairs—those whom anomalies hastened to calamity and defeat are probably not few; the way of expiation and avoidance—if it is not what one has examined carefully—then for the nonce ought to select the winning pattern among human affairs and ponder the long plan for altars and grain; then the realm will be greatly fortunate and a fair name can be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Scan past and present: ill omens have rushed many regimes to ruin. Exorcism rarely clarifies anything—better weigh practical policy and the dynasty's long-term survival; that brings fortune to the realm and keeps one's reputation intact.

sentences.zh: 若安西盛意已耳，不能安于武昌，但得近移夏口，則其次也。

translations.literal: If the Western Pacifier's earnest intent is already merely that he cannot be at peace in Wuchang—only obtaining a near shift to Xiakou—that is the next choice.
translations.idiomatic: If the Western Pacifier truly cannot stay easy at Wuchang, shifting slightly downstream to Xiakou would be an acceptable compromise.

sentences.zh: 樂鄉之舉，咸謂不可。

translations.literal: The Lexiang undertaking—all said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone agrees the Lexiang plan will not do.

sentences.zh: 願將軍體國為家，固審此舉。

translations.literal: I wish the general will embody the state as family and firmly examine this undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to weigh the realm as your own household and judge this move with cold clarity.

sentences.zh: 時朝議亦不允，翼遂不移鎮。

translations.literal: At the time court deliberation also did not approve; Yi thereupon did not shift the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion sided against the move, so Yu Yi dropped the relocation.

sentences.zh: 述出補臨海太守，遷建威將軍、會稽內史。

translations.literal: Shu went out to supplement as governor of Linhai; he was promoted general who establishes might and interior minister of Guiji.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu left the capital to become governor of Linhai, then rose to general of the army that establishes might and interior governor of Guiji.

sentences.zh: 蒞政清肅，終日無事。

translations.literal: Presiding over governance, clear and austere; all day nothing happened.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was spare and orderly—days passed without needless bustle.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: On mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，代殷浩為揚州刺史，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he replaced Yin Hao as inspector of Yangzhou; further he was appointed general who conquers the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he succeeded Yin Hao as Yangzhou provincial inspector and received the additional title general who conquers the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 初至，主簿請諱。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, the chief clerk requested taboo [names].
translations.idiomatic: On first taking up the post, his chief clerk asked which names to avoid.

sentences.zh: 報曰：「亡祖先君，名播海內，遠近所知；

translations.literal: He replied, saying, 'My late grandfather and father—their names spread within the seas; known to far and near.'
translations.idiomatic: He answered, 'My late grandfather and father were famous throughout the realm—everyone knows their names.'

sentences.zh: 內諱不出門，餘無所諱。

translations.literal: Inner taboos do not go out the gate; for the rest there is nothing tabooed.'
translations.idiomatic: Private names stay within the household; beyond that I impose no taboos.'

sentences.zh: 」尋加中書監，固讓，經年不拜。

translations.literal: Soon he was added as overseer of the masters of writing; he firmly declined; a full year he did not accept appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named overseer of the palace writers but firmly declined and held out a full year without taking the post.

sentences.zh: 復加征虜將軍，進都督揚州徐州之琅邪諸軍事、衛將軍、並冀幽平四州大中正，刺史如故。

translations.literal: Further he was appointed general who conquers the barbarians; advanced to area commander for Yangzhou, Xuzhou, and Langye military affairs, guard general, and concurrently senior rectifier for Ji, You, and Ping four prefectures; inspector as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was again named general who conquers the barbarians, promoted to commander of Yangzhou, Xuzhou, and Langye forces, appointed guard general, and made concurrent senior rectifier for Ji, You, and Ping—while retaining his inspector post.

sentences.zh: 尋遷散騎常侍、尚書令，將軍如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to attendant at large and regular attendant, director of the masters of writing; general as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became imperial attendant and director of the masters of writing, keeping his military title.

sentences.zh: 述每受職，不為虛讓，其有所辭，必於不受。

translations.literal: Whenever Shu received office, he did not perform empty yielding; when he had something to decline, it was invariably in [cases of] not accepting.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu never performed hollow refusals when accepting posts; if he declined, he truly meant to refuse.

sentences.zh: 至是，子坦之諫，以為故事應讓。

translations.literal: At this time his son Tanzhi remonstrated, thinking precedent required yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Then his son Wang Tanzhi urged him, citing precedent that one should demur.

sentences.zh: 述曰：「汝謂我不堪邪？

translations.literal: Shu said, 'You consider me not competent?'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu asked, 'Do you think I cannot handle the office?'

sentences.zh: 」坦之曰：「非也。

translations.literal: Tanzhi said, 'It is not so.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi replied, 'No.'

sentences.zh: 但克讓自美事耳。

translations.literal: Only that restrained yielding is itself a beautiful thing.'
translations.idiomatic: Only that graceful self-effacement is admirable in itself.'

sentences.zh: 」述曰：「既-{云}-堪，何為復讓！

translations.literal: Shu said, 'Since it is already said [I am] competent—why again yield!'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu retorted, 'If I am fit for the role, why put on a show of refusing?'

sentences.zh: 人言汝勝我，定不及也。

translations.literal: People say you surpass me—that is certainly not so.
translations.idiomatic: People claim you outshine me—they are mistaken.

sentences.zh: 」坦之為桓溫長史。

translations.literal: Tanzhi became Huan Wen's chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi served as chief clerk to Huan Wen.

sentences.zh: 溫欲為子求婚於坦之。

translations.literal: Wen wished to seek marriage for his son with Tanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen wanted to arrange a marriage between his son and Wang Tanzhi's daughter.

sentences.zh: 及還家省父，而述愛坦之。

translations.literal: When [Tanzhi] returned home to visit his father, Shu loved Tanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tanzhi went home to see his father, Wang Shu doted on him.

sentences.zh: 雖長大，猶抱置膝上。

translations.literal: Although grown large, still [Shu] hugged and placed him on his knees.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Tanzhi was fully grown, Wang Shu would still pull him onto his lap.

sentences.zh: 坦之因言溫意。

translations.literal: Tanzhi thereupon spoke Wen's intention.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi then raised Huan Wen's proposal.

sentences.zh: 述大怒，遽排下，曰：「汝竟癡邪！

translations.literal: Shu greatly raged; abruptly pushed him down; said, 'You are ultimately a fool!'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu flared with anger, pushed him off his knees, and shouted, 'Have you lost your mind?'

sentences.zh: 詎可畏溫面而以女妻兵也。

translations.literal: How can one fear Wen's face and thereby give a daughter to marry a soldier!'
translations.idiomatic: Would you truckle to Huan Wen's temper and marry your daughter into a soldier's house!'

sentences.zh: 」坦之乃辭以他故。

translations.literal: Tanzhi thereupon declined with another reason.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi declined on other grounds.

sentences.zh: 溫曰：「此尊君不肯耳。

translations.literal: Wen said, 'This is only [because] your honoured father would not.'
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen said, 'Your father simply refused.'

sentences.zh: 」遂止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter ended there.

sentences.zh: 簡文帝每言述才既不長，直以真率便敵人耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Jianwen often said Shu's talent was not long; simply by genuine straightforwardness he matched others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jianwen often remarked that Wang Shu's gifts were modest—his blunt sincerity alone made him a match for anyone.

sentences.zh: 謝安亦歎美之。

translations.literal: Xie An also sighed in admiration of him.
translations.idiomatic: Xie An praised him as well.

sentences.zh: 初，述家貧。

translations.literal: Formerly Shu's household was poor.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days Wang Shu's family was destitute.

sentences.zh: 求試宛陵令。

translations.literal: He sought probation as magistrate of Wanling.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to serve a probationary term as magistrate of Wanling.

sentences.zh: 頗受贈遺。

translations.literal: He rather received gifts and largesse.
translations.idiomatic: He accepted a fair number of gifts.

sentences.zh: 而修傢俱，為州司所檢，有一千三百條。

translations.literal: Further he repaired household furnishings; he was inspected by the provincial office—there were one thousand three hundred items.
translations.idiomatic: When he refurbished his household goods, provincial auditors cited him on thirteen hundred counts.

sentences.zh: 王導使謂之曰：「名父之子不患無祿，屈臨小縣，甚不宜耳。

translations.literal: Wang Dao sent to tell him, saying, 'The son of a renowned father does not worry about lacking salary; bending to attend a small county is very improper.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao sent word: 'A son of an eminent house need never fear poverty—demeaning yourself in a minor county is hardly fitting.'

sentences.zh: 」述答曰：「足自當止。

translations.literal: Shu answered, saying, 'It is enough—it will stop of itself.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu replied, 'I have enough—it will stop on its own.'

sentences.zh: 時人未之達也。

translations.literal: Men of the time did not penetrate this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries failed to grasp his meaning.'

sentences.zh: 」比後屢居州郡，清潔絕倫，祿賜皆散之親故，宅宇舊物不革於昔，始為當時所歎。

translations.literal: Compared afterward [when] repeatedly dwelling in provinces and commanderies—pure and clean beyond comparison—salary and gifts he all scattered to kin and old friends; house halls and old goods were not altered from former times—only then was he sighed over by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after successive provincial posts of impeccable honesty, he poured salary and imperial gifts into helping kin and friends while leaving his house unchanged—then everyone marvelled at the man they had misjudged.

sentences.zh: 但性急為累。

translations.literal: Only quick temper became a burden.
translations.idiomatic: His quick temper was his only flaw.

sentences.zh: 嘗食雞子，以箸刺之，不得，便大怒擲地。

translations.literal: Once eating eggs, he stabbed them with chopsticks; not obtaining [the bite], then greatly enraged he threw them on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Once, failing to spear a boiled egg with his chopsticks, he flew into a rage and hurled it down.

sentences.zh: 雞子圓轉不止，便下床以屐齒踏之，又不得。

translations.literal: The egg rolled round without stopping; then he went down from the bed and used clog-teeth to tread it—again did not obtain.
translations.idiomatic: The egg spun away; he jumped down and tried to crush it with his clog—still without success.

sentences.zh: 瞋甚，掇內口中，齧破而吐之。

translations.literal: Very angry, he picked it up and put it inside his mouth, bit it broken and spat it out.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, he stuffed it into his mouth, bit through it, and spat it out.

sentences.zh: 既躋重位，每以柔克為用。

translations.literal: Having already ascended to weighty position, he always used yielding to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated to high office he habitually answered force with yielding patience.

sentences.zh: 謝奕性粗，嘗忿述，極言罵之。

translations.literal: Xie Yi by nature was coarse; once he resented Shu and with utmost words reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: The blunt Xie Yi once vented his spite on Wang Shu with torrents of abuse.

sentences.zh: 述無所應，面壁而已，居半日，奕去，始復坐。

translations.literal: Shu responded to nothing; faced the wall only; dwelling half a day, Yi departed; only then did he again sit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu said nothing and stared at the wall for hours until Xie left; only then did he return to his seat.

sentences.zh: 人以此稱之。

translations.literal: People on this account praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers praised him for that restraint.

sentences.zh: ，以年迫懸車，上疏乞骸骨，曰：「臣曾祖父魏司空昶白箋于文皇帝曰：'昔與南陽宗世林共為東宮官屬。

translations.literal: [Fragment:] , because age pressed toward hanging-up-the-cart, submitted memorial begging bones for returning, saying: 'Your subject's great-grandfather, Wei Minister of Works Chang, submitted a plain note to Emperor Wen, saying: Formerly with Zong Shilin of Nanyang together were eastern palace office retinue.'
translations.idiomatic: [Text opens mid-sentence.] With age pressing him toward retirement, he memorialized to surrender office, quoting his great-grandfather Wang Chang's letter to Emperor Wen of Wei: 'Once Zong Shilin of Nanyang and I both served the heir apparent.'

sentences.zh: 世林少得好名，州裏瞻敬。

translations.literal: Shilin in youth obtained good reputation; the province looked up in reverence.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Zong Shilin won admiration; the province looked up to him.

sentences.zh: 及其年老，汲汲自勵，恐見廢棄，時人咸共笑之。

translations.literal: When he reached old age, urgently he urged himself, fearing being seen cast aside; men of the time all together laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he scrambled to stay relevant, terrified of being cast aside—everyone laughed.

sentences.zh: 若天假其壽，致仕之年，不為此公婆娑之事。

translations.literal: If Heaven lent him years, at the year of handing over office, he would not do these old-woman shuffling affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: Had Heaven granted him longer life, he would not have debased himself so in retirement.'

sentences.zh: '情旨慷慨，深所鄙薄。

translations.literal: The feeling's intent was stirring and generous—deeply what I despise and hold cheap.'
translations.idiomatic: That fervent tone repelled me.'

sentences.zh: 雖是箋書，乃實訓誡。

translations.literal: Although it is a note document, it is really instruction and warning.'
translations.idiomatic: Though only a letter, it was meant as a lasting lesson.'

sentences.zh: 臣忝端右，而以疾患，禮敬廢替。

translations.literal: Your subject disgraces the right end [high office]; yet because of illness and ailment, ritual reverence is abandoned and replaced.'
translations.idiomatic: I shame the chief minister's seat yet illness keeps me from performing the proper courtesies.'

sentences.zh: 猶謂可有差理，日復一日，而年衰疾痼，永無復瞻華幄之期。

translations.literal: Still I thought there could be improving principle; day repeats day; yet years decline and sickness is chronic—forever no again gazing on splendid canopy's season.'
translations.idiomatic: I hoped to recover in time, but days repeat and my chronic malady bars me forever from the imperial hall.'

sentences.zh: 乞奉先誡，歸老丘園。

translations.literal: I beg to follow prior warning and return old among hills and gardens.'
translations.idiomatic: I beg leave to heed my ancestor's warning and retire to the hills.'

sentences.zh: 」不許。

translations.literal: Not permitted.'
translations.idiomatic: The throne refused.'

sentences.zh: 述竟不起。

translations.literal: Shu ultimately did not rise [to office].
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu never returned to active duty.

sentences.zh: 三年卒，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the third year he died; at the time age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of the era at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 初，桓溫平洛陽，議欲遷都，朝廷憂懼，將遣侍中止之。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Huan Wen pacified Luoyang, deliberation wished to shift the capital; court worried and feared; was about to send attendant attendants to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Wen took Luoyang, talk of moving the capital terrified the court, which prepared to send chamberlains to dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 述曰：「溫欲以虛聲威朝廷，非事實也。

translations.literal: Shu said: 'Wen wishes by empty reputation to awe court—it is not factual reality.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu said, 'Huan Wen only wants to cow the court with bluster—he has no serious plan.'

sentences.zh: 但從之，自無所至。

translations.literal: Only follow him—of itself there will be nothing reached.'
translations.idiomatic: Humour him and nothing will come of it.'

sentences.zh: 」事果不行。

translations.literal: The affair indeed did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal collapsed.

sentences.zh: 又議欲移洛陽鐘虡，述曰：「永嘉不競，暫都江左。

translations.literal: Further deliberation wished to move Luoyang's bells and stands; Shu said: 'Yongjia could not compete; temporarily lodged capital east of the river.'
translations.idiomatic: When officials debated shipping the Luoyang bells east, Wang Shu said, 'After Yongjia we merely camped south of the river.'

sentences.zh: 方當蕩平區宇，旋軫舊京。

translations.literal: Just when we ought to sweep-level the realm and turn the axletree back to the old capital.'
translations.idiomatic: We mean to reconquer the realm and wheel back to the ancient capital.'

sentences.zh: 若其不耳，宜改遷園陵。

translations.literal: If it is not thus, ought to alter and shift the imperial tombs.'
translations.idiomatic: If not, relocate the imperial tombs instead.'

sentences.zh: 不應先事鐘虡。

translations.literal: One ought not first attend to bells and stands.'
translations.idiomatic: Do not fuss over ritual bells first.'

sentences.zh: 」溫竟無以奪之。

translations.literal: Wen ultimately had nothing wherewith to wrest it from him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Wen could find no answer.

sentences.zh: 追贈侍中、驃騎將軍、開府，諡曰穆，以避穆帝，改曰簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded attendant-in-ordinary, general of agile cavalry, establishment of a headquarters; posthumous title said Mu; because of avoiding Emperor Mu, changed to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named attendant-in-ordinary, general of agile cavalry, with independent command; his posthumous epithet was first Mu, then changed to Jian to avoid Emperor Mu's taboo.

sentences.zh: 子坦之嗣。

translations.literal: His son Tanzhi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi inherited his title.

translations.literal: Equals sign (continuity marker in source text).

sentences.zh: 述子坦之

translations.literal: Shu's son Tanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi (son of Wang Shu)

sentences.zh: =坦之字文度。

translations.idiomatic: He rose through military aide and secretariat adviser to marshal and received the additional title attendant at large.

translations.idiomatic: He left court to become chief clerk to Huan Wen as grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 尋以父憂去職，服闋。

translations.literal: Soon because of father's mourning he left office; when mourning ended.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned for his father's death and returned once mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 徵拜侍中，襲父爵。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed attendant-in-ordinary; inherited father's noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as attendant-in-ordinary, he succeeded to his father's noble title.

sentences.zh: 海西公廢，領左衛將軍。

translations.idiomatic: After Duke Ai of Haixi was deposed, Wang Tanzhi commanded the Left Guard.

translations.idiomatic: He also served as senior rectifier for his home province.

translations.idiomatic: As Emperor Jianwen lay dying, an edict instructed Huan Wen to follow the Duke of Zhou's regency precedent.

sentences.zh: 坦之自持詔入，於帝前毀之。

translations.literal: Tanzhi himself held the edict and entered; before the emperor tore it up.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi carried the edict in and tore it up before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天下，儻來之運，卿何所嫌！

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'All under Heaven—adventitious coming fortune—what do you dislike!'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'The realm fell into your lap—why shrink from it?'

sentences.zh: 」帝乃使坦之改詔焉。

translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Wang Tanzhi rewrite the edict.

sentences.zh: 溫薨，坦之與謝安共輔幼主，遷中書令，領丹陽尹。

translations.idiomatic: After Huan Wen died, Wang Tanzhi and Xie An co-regented for the boy emperor; Wang Tanzhi became director of the palace secretariat and concurrent governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 俄授都督徐兗青三州諸軍事、北中郎將、徐兗二州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.idiomatic: He was soon named commander of Xu, Yan, and Qing forces, general of the northern centre, concurrent inspector of Xu and Yan, and stationed at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 將之鎮，上表曰：

translations.idiomatic: Before leaving for his post he memorialized:

translations.literal: [Wiki template opening.] Your subject hears that the way of a lord takes filial reverence as root; facing and overseeing the four seas takes delegation as honour.

sentences.zh: 恭順無為，則盛德日新；

translations.literal: Respectful submission and non-action—then abundant virtue daily renews.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful restraint without meddling renews your virtue daily.

sentences.zh: 親杖賢能，則政道邕睦。

translations.literal: Personally leaning on the worthy and able—then the way of governance is harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Rely on worthy men and your government stays harmonious.

sentences.zh: 昔周成、漢昭，並以幼年纂承大統。

translations.literal: Formerly Cheng of Zhou and Zhao of Han, both in youth succeeded to the great bond.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng of Zhou and Emperor Zhao of Han both inherited the throne as boys.

sentences.zh: 當時天下未為無難，終能顯揚祖考，保安社稷，蓋尊尊親親，信納大臣之所致也。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was not without difficulty; in the end able to display and raise ancestors, pacify and guard altars and grain—this was caused by honouring the honoured, loving the kin, faithfully receiving great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Their age was no easier than ours, yet they glorified their forebears and secured the state—because they honoured hierarchy, cherished kin, and trusted their chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 伏維陛下誕奇秀之姿，稟生知之量，春秋尚富，涉道未廣，方須訓導以成天德。

translations.literal: Prostrate I consider Your Majesty's bearing of marvellous excellence's posture, endowed with born-knowing's measure; spring and autumn are still rich; traversing the Way is not yet broad—just now must training and guidance complete heaven's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's talents are extraordinary and your years still few—the Way lies ahead and will ripen only through steady instruction.

sentences.zh: 皇太后仁淑之體，過於三母，先帝奉事積年，每稱聖明。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's benevolent and virtuous substance surpasses the three mothers; the late emperor served affairs accumulated years; always praised sagely clarity.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's kindness exceeds the exemplary mothers of antiquity; the late emperor served her for years and ever called her wise.

sentences.zh: 臣願奉事之心，便當自同孝宗；

translations.literal: Your subject's wish to serve affairs' heart—then ought itself to match the filial ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant would serve her with the same devotion owed to a revered father.

sentences.zh: 太后慈愛之隆，亦不必異所生。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's loving kindness's loftiness—also need not differ from those born.
translations.idiomatic: Her motherly love need not shy away from natural affection.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王、餘姚主及諸皇女，宜朝夕定省，承受教誨，導習儀刑，以成景仰恭敬之美，不可以屬非至親，自為疏疑。

translations.literal: The Prince of Langye, the Princess of Yuyao, and the various imperial daughters—ought morning and evening attend and inquire, receive and bear instruction and teaching, guide and practise deportment and models, thereby complete the beauty of revering and looking up respectfully; one cannot because ties are not ultimate kin make oneself distant and doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: You should visit the Prince of Langye, the Princess of Yuyao, and your sisters morning and night, learn deportment at their knees, and nurture reverence—do not treat them as distant kin and breed suspicion.

sentences.zh: 昔肅祖崩殂，成康幼沖，事無大小，必諮丞相導，所以克就聖德，實此之由，今僕射臣安、中軍臣沖，人望具瞻，社稷之臣。

translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Su died, Emperors Cheng and Kang were infants and looked to Wang Dao for every decision—that made their virtue possible. Today Xie An as vice-director and Huan Chong commanding the central army hold the realm's trust.

sentences.zh: 且受遇先帝，綢繆繾綣，並志竭忠貞，盡心盡力，歸誠陛下，以報先帝。

translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, every move you make

translations.idiomatic: They stand to you as the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao to the boy king, as Huo Guang to Han, as Emperor Yuan to Wang Dao.

translations.idiomatic: Though Huan Chong is posted away, the roads are short enough for counsel within a day or two—consult him in detail so nothing is missed.

translations.literal: Further Heaven's hearing, though keen—if not opened, not broad.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven may hear all, yet without counsel your perspective stays narrow.

sentences.zh: 群情雖忠，不引不盡。

translations.literal: The multitude's feelings, though loyal—if not drawn forth, not exhausted.

sentences.zh: 宜數引侍臣，詢求讜言。

translations.literal: Ought repeatedly summon attendant ministers; inquire seeking straightforward words.
translations.idiomatic: Summon your attendants often and invite blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 平易之世，有道之主猶尚誡懼，日昃不倦；

translations.literal: In easy-level ages, lords who had the Way still esteemed caution and fear; sun declining without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Even sage kings in peaceful times stayed wary past noon.

sentences.zh: 況今艱難理盡，慮經安危，祖宗之基系之陛下，不可不精心務道，以申先帝堯舜之風。

translations.literal: Moreover now hardship's principle is exhausted; anxieties traverse peril and safety; ancestors' foundation hangs on Your Majesty—cannot fail to concentrate spirit and pursue the Way, thereby extend the late emperor's Yao-Shun wind.
translations.idiomatic: Our age is perilous—the ancestral legacy rests on you; you must devote yourself to the Way and carry forward the late emperor's aspirations to emulate Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 可不敬修至德，以保宣元天地之祚？

translations.idiomatic: Will you not cultivate supreme virtue to safeguard the fortune won by Xuandi and Yuandi?'

translations.idiomatic: Honour each man's bent and his achievement ripens like pine and bamboo in winter cold.'

translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi was close to the monk Zhu Fashi and often debated karma with him.

translations.idiomatic: They agreed that whoever died first would report back.

translations.idiomatic: Wang Tanzhi died soon after at forty-six.

sentences.zh: 臨終，與謝安、桓沖書，言不及私，惟憂國家之事，朝野甚痛惜之。

translations.literal: Facing end, with Xie An, Huan Chong letters—speech did not reach private matters; only worried state's affairs; court and wild greatly painful regret for him.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he wrote to Xie An and Huan Chong of nothing personal—only the state—and court and countryside mourned him.

translations.idiomatic: He died before thirty and was posthumously named attendant at large.
