translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai inherited his father's title; Wang Yu rose to marshal on the agile-cavalry staff and received the additional title general who aids the state.

sentences.zh: 愷太元末為侍中，領右衛將軍，多所獻替。

translations.literal: Kai at the end of Taiyuan was attendant-in-ordinary, heading general of the right guard; many presented replacements.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Taiyuan era Wang Kai served as attendant-in-ordinary and commanded the Right Guard, offering frequent counsel.

sentences.zh: 兄弟貴盛，當時莫比。

translations.literal: Brothers noble and flourishing; of the age none compared.
translations.idiomatic: No brothers of their generation matched their combined power.

sentences.zh: 及王恭等討國寶，愷、愉並請解職。

translations.literal: When Wang Gong and others attacked Guobao, Kai and Yu together requested release from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Gong moved against Wang Guobao, both Wang Kai and Wang Yu asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 以與國寶異生，又素不協，故得免禍。

translations.literal: Because with Guobao different birth; further by nature not harmonious—therefore obtained avoidance of calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Different mothers and long-standing estrangement from Guobao spared them.

sentences.zh: 國寶既死，出愷為吳郡內史，愉為江州刺史、都督豫州四郡、輔國將軍、假節。

translations.literal: When Guobao had died, Kai went out as interior minister of Wu commandery; Yu became inspector of Jiangzhou, area commander of Yuzhou four commanderies, general who aids the state, borrowed insignia.
translations.idiomatic: After Guobao died, Wang Kai became interior governor of Wu while Wang Yu became inspector of Jiangzhou, commander over four Yuzhou commands, general who aids the state, with ceremonial credentials.

sentences.zh: 未幾，征愷為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Before long, summoned Kai as governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Kai was recalled as governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 及桓玄等至江寧，愷令兵守石頭。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan and others reached Jiangning, Kai ordered soldiers to guard Stone Citadel.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan reached Jiangning, Wang Kai stationed troops at Stone Citadel.

sentences.zh: 俄而玄等走，復為吳郡。

translations.literal: Soon Xuan and others fled; [Kai] again became Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan soon withdrew and Wang Kai returned as governor of Wu.

sentences.zh: 病卒，追贈太常。

translations.literal: Sick died; posthumously awarded chamberlain of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness and was posthumously named chamberlain of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 愉至鎮，未幾，殷仲堪、桓玄、楊佺期舉兵應王恭，乘流奄至。

translations.literal: When Yu reached the garrison, before long Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan, Yang Quanqi raised troops responding to Wang Gong; riding the current suddenly arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after Wang Yu reached his post, Yin Zhongkan, Huan Xuan, and Yang Quanqi mobilized for Wang Gong and swept downstream upon him.

sentences.zh: 愉既無備，惶遽奔臨川，為玄所得。

translations.literal: Yu having no preparation, in panic fled to Linchuan; was captured by Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Caught unprepared, Wang Yu fled toward Linchuan and fell into Huan Xuan's hands.

sentences.zh: 玄盟于尋陽，以愉置壇所，愉甚恥之。

translations.literal: Xuan covenanted at Xunyang; using Yu placed at altar site; Yu greatly shamed it.
translations.idiomatic: At the Xunyang league Huan Xuan left Wang Yu standing by the altar—a humiliation Wang deeply resented.

sentences.zh: 及事解，除會稽內史。

translations.literal: When the affair was resolved, appointed interior minister of Guiji.
translations.idiomatic: After peace returned he was named interior governor of Guiji.

sentences.zh: 玄篡位，以為尚書僕射。

translations.literal: Xuan usurped the throne; appointed [Yu] superintendent of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan seized the throne he made Wang Yu vice-director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 劉裕義旗建，加前將軍。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu's righteous banner was raised, added general of the van.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu raised the loyalist cause Wang Yu received the additional title general of the van.

sentences.zh: 愉既桓氏婿，父子寵貴，又嘗輕侮劉裕，心不自安，潛結司州刺史溫詳，謀作亂，事泄，被誅，子孫十餘人皆伏法。

translations.literal: Yu being Huan clan's son-in-law, father and sons favoured and noble; further once slighted and insulted Liu Yu—heart not self at ease; secretly allied with inspector of Sizhou Wen Xiang; plotted to raise rebellion; affair leaked; was executed; sons and grandsons more than ten persons all submitted to law.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu was a Huan in-law; father and son had grown arrogant and once slighted Liu Yu. Fear drove him to plot with Wen Xiang, inspector of Sizhou; the plot leaked and he was executed along with over ten kin.

translations.literal: Equals sign (continuity marker in source text).

sentences.zh: 愉弟國寶

translations.literal: Yu's younger brother Guobao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao (younger brother of Wang Yu)

sentences.zh: =國寶少無士操，不修廉隅。

translations.literal: = Guobao in youth had no gentleman's conduct; did not cultivate corners of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao lacked scholarly scruples in youth and kept no moral boundaries.

sentences.zh: 婦父謝安惡其傾側，每抑而不用。

translations.literal: Wife's father Xie An hated his leaning and tilting; always suppressed and did not use.
translations.idiomatic: His father-in-law Xie An despised his shiftiness and repeatedly blocked his promotion.

sentences.zh: 除尚書郎。

translations.literal: Appointed gentleman of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed secretary in the masters-of-writing department.

sentences.zh: 國寶以中興膏腴之族，惟作吏部，不為余曹郎，甚怨望，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Guobao because restoration fat-soil clan—only made personnel bureau; did not become other bureau gentlemen—greatly resentful; firmly declined not accepting.
translations.idiomatic: As scion of a premier restoration clan he expected the personnel bureau, not a lesser bureau—he refused the post in resentment.

sentences.zh: 從妹為會稽王道子妃，由是與道子遊處，遂間毀安焉。

translations.literal: A cousin younger sister was Prince of Guiji Daozi's consort; thereupon with Daozi travelled and dwelt; thereupon slandered An.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin was consort to Prince Sima Daozi of Guiji, so he courted Daozi and used the tie to slander Xie An.

sentences.zh: 及道子輔政，以為秘書丞。

translations.literal: When Daozi aided governance, appointed [him] assistant director of the palace library.
translations.idiomatic: When Daozi began directing policy he named Wang Guobao assistant director of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 俄遷琅邪內史，領堂邑太守，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: Soon transferred interior minister of Langye, concurrently governor of Tangyi, added general who aids the state.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became interior governor of Langye, concurrent governor of Tangyi, with the additional title general who aids the state.

sentences.zh: 人補侍中，遷中書令、中領軍，與道子持威權，扇動內外。

translations.literal: Person supplemented attendant-in-ordinary; transferred director of palace writers, central army commander; with Daozi wielded awesome power; fanned and moved inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: He moved up to attendant-in-ordinary, then director of the palace secretariat and central army commander, sharing Daozi's grip on power and swaying court and countryside.

sentences.zh: 中書郎范寧，國寶舅也，儒雅方直，疾其阿諛，勸孝武帝黜之。

translations.literal: Gentleman of palace writers Fan Ning—Guobao's maternal uncle—refined and Ru, square and straight; hated his flattery; urged Emperor Xiaowu to dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ning of the secretariat—Guobao's uncle—was learned and upright; loathing the flattery he urged Emperor Xiaowu to dismiss Guobao.

sentences.zh: 國寶乃使陳郡袁悅之因尼支妙音致書與太子母陳淑媛，說國寶忠謹，宜見親信。

translations.literal: Guobao thereupon ordered Yuan Yuezhi of Chen command through nun Zhi Miaoyin to deliver letter to crown prince's mother Chen Shuyuan, explaining Guobao loyal and careful—ought be seen trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao had Yuan Yuezhi smuggle a letter via the nun Zhi Miaoyin to the crown prince's mother, praising his loyalty to win favour.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，托以他罪殺悅之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew it; on pretext of another crime killed Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of it and executed Yuan Yuezhi on another charge.

sentences.zh: 國寶大懼，遂因道子譖毀寧，寧由是出為豫章太守。

translations.literal: Guobao greatly feared; thereupon through Daozi slandered and destroyed Ning; Ning thereby went out as governor of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Guobao used Daozi to defame Fan Ning, who was banished to Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 及弟忱卒，國寶自表求解職迎母。

translations.literal: When younger brother Chen died, Guobao himself memorialized requesting release from office to welcome mother.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother Wang Chen died Guobao asked leave to fetch his mother.

sentences.zh: 並奔忱喪。

translations.literal: Together rushed to Chen's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: They hurried together to Wang Chen's funeral.

sentences.zh: 詔特賜假，而盤桓不時進發，為御史中丞褚粲所奏。

translations.literal: An edict specially granted leave, yet he lingered and did not timely advance and depart—was impeached by metropolitan shepherd Chu Can.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him leave, but he delayed departure and Chu Can, metropolitan shepherd, impeached him.

sentences.zh: 國寶懼罪，衣女子衣，托為王家婢，詣道子告其事。

translations.literal: Guobao feared punishment; clothed in women's clothes; pretended to be a Wang household maid; went to Daozi and reported the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Guobao, terrified of punishment, dressed as a woman, posed as a Wang family servant, and appealed to Sima Daozi.

sentences.zh: 道子言之於帝，故得原。

translations.literal: Daozi spoke of it to the emperor; therefore obtained pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi spoke to the emperor and secured his pardon.

sentences.zh: 後驃騎參軍王徽請國寶同宴，國寶素驕貴使酒，怒尚書左丞祖台之，攘袂大呼，以盤盞樂器擲台之，台之不敢言，復為粲所彈。

translations.literal: Later army adjutant to agile cavalry Wang Hui invited Guobao to share a banquet; Guobao by nature proud and noble urged wine; was angry at masters of writing left aide Zu Taizhi; pushed sleeves and loudly shouted; with plates, cups, and musical instruments threw at Taizhi; Taizhi did not dare speak—again was impeached by Can.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hui invited Wang Guobao to drink, Guobao—drunk and arrogant—berated Zu Taizhi and threw dishes at him; Zu stayed silent, and Chu Can impeached Guobao again.

sentences.zh: 詔以國寶縱肆情性，甚不可長，台之懦弱，非監司體，並坐免官。

translations.literal: Edict because Guobao indulged and unleashed disposition—greatly cannot be allowed to grow; Taizhi cowardly weak—not inspector's substance—together seated dismissed office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict blamed Guobao's indulgence and Zu's timidity—both were stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復職，愈驕蹇不遵法度。

translations.literal: Shortly, restored office—more arrogant and stubborn, did not observe statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon reinstated, he grew more wilful and lawless.

sentences.zh: 起齋侔清暑殿，帝惡其僭侈。

translations.literal: Raised a chapel matching the Cool Summer Hall—the emperor hated its presumptuous extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: He built a chapel rivalling the Cool Summer Hall—an extravagance that disgusted the emperor.

sentences.zh: 國寶懼，遂諂媚於帝，而頗疏道子。

translations.literal: Guobao feared; thereupon flattered the emperor; and rather estranged Daozi.
translations.idiomatic: Frightened, he courted the emperor and drifted from Daozi.

sentences.zh: 道子大怒，嘗於內省面責國寶，以劍擲之，舊好盡矣。

translations.literal: Daozi greatly raged; once in inner bureau faced and rebuked Guobao; with sword threw at him—old friendship utterly ended.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi raged and once rebuked Guobao inside the palace, even throwing a sword at him—their alliance ended.

sentences.zh: 是時王雅亦有寵，薦王珣於帝。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Ya also had favour; recommended Wang Xun to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya enjoyed favour then and recommended Wang Xun to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝夜與國寶及雅宴，帝微有酒，令召珣，將至，國寶自知才出珣下，恐至，傾其寵，因曰：「王珣當今名流，不可以酒色見。

translations.literal: The emperor at night with Guobao and Ya feasted; the emperor slightly had wine; ordered summon Xun; about to arrive—Guobao himself knew talent came out below Xun; feared arrival would overturn his favour; thereupon said: 'Wang Xun is today's noted stream—cannot with wine and colour be seen.'
translations.idiomatic: During a night banquet the emperor, somewhat drunk, summoned Wang Xun. Guobao knew himself inferior and feared losing favour, so he said, 'Wang Xun is a leading gentleman—do not receive him amid wine and revelry.'

sentences.zh: 」帝遂止，而以國寶為忠。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped; and took Guobao as loyal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor cancelled the summons and deemed Guobao loyal.

sentences.zh: 將納國寶女為琅邪王妃，未婚，而帝崩。

translations.literal: About to take Guobao's daughter as Langye prince's consort—not yet married, yet the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: He had meant to marry Guobao's daughter to the Prince of Langye, but the emperor died before the wedding.

sentences.zh: 安帝即位，國寶復事道子，進從祖弟緒為琅邪內史，亦以佞邪見知。

translations.literal: When Emperor An mounted the throne, Guobao again served Daozi; advanced cousin younger brother Xu as interior minister of Langye—also by flattery and wickedness was known.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor An, Wang Guobao again served Daozi and installed his cousin Wang Xu as interior governor of Langye—another sycophant.

sentences.zh: 道子復惑之，倚為心腹，並為時之所疾。

translations.literal: Daozi again was deluded by them; relied on them as heart and belly—together were what the age despised.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi trusted them as intimates, and both men were loathed.

sentences.zh: 國寶遂參管朝權，威震內外。

translations.literal: Guobao thereupon participated in managing court power—awe shook inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao seized court power and dominated capital and provinces.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Transferred left superintendent of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left vice-director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 領選，加後將軍、丹陽尹，道子悉以東宮兵配之。

translations.literal: Headed selections; added general of the rear, governor of Danyang; Daozi entirely with heir-apparent's troops assigned him.
translations.idiomatic: He directed appointments, added the title general of the rear and governor of Danyang, and Daozi gave him the heir apparent's troops.

sentences.zh: 時王恭與殷仲堪並以才器，各居名籓。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan both by talent and implements—each dwelt famous screens.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong and Yin Zhongkan held prominent provincial commands.

sentences.zh: 恭惡道子、國寶亂政，屢有憂國之言。

translations.literal: Gong hated Daozi and Guobao disordering governance—repeatedly had anxious-for-state words.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong loathed Daozi and Guobao's misrule and often voiced concern for the realm.

sentences.zh: 道子等亦深忌憚之，將謀去其兵。

translations.literal: Daozi and others also deeply dreaded them—were about to plot removing their troops.
translations.idiomatic: Daozi feared them and plotted to strip their armies.

sentences.zh: 未及行，而恭檄至，以討國寶為名，國寶惶遽不知所為。

translations.literal: Before reaching execution—yet Gong's proclamation arrived—using attacking Guobao as name—Guobao panic-stricken—did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Before the plan moved, Wang Gong's manifesto arrived demanding Guobao's head; Guobao panicked.

sentences.zh: 緒說國寶，令矯道子命，召王珣、車胤殺之，以除群望，因挾主相以討諸侯。

translations.literal: Xu persuaded Guobao—ordered forge Daozi's command—summon Wang Xun, Che Yin kill them—thereby remove group's expectations—thereby clasp lord and chancellor to attack the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xu urged Guobao to forge Daozi's order, summon Wang Xun and Che Yin to kill them, silence rivals, then coerce emperor and minister against the provinces.

sentences.zh: 國寶許之。

translations.literal: Guobao assented.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao agreed.

sentences.zh: 珣、胤既至，而不敢害，反問計於珣。

translations.literal: Xun, Yin having arrived—yet did not dare harm—turned and asked plan of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun and Yin arrived, Guobao dared not kill them and asked Xun for advice.

sentences.zh: 珣勸國寶放兵權以迎恭，國寶信之。

translations.literal: Xun urged Guobao to release military authority to welcome Gong—Guobao trusted it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun urged him to yield command to placate Wang Gong, and Guobao believed him.

sentences.zh: 語在《珣傳》。

translations.literal: The words are in 'Xun's biography.'
translations.idiomatic: Details appear in the biography of Wang Xun.

sentences.zh: 又問計於胤，胤曰：「南北同舉，而荊州未至，若朝廷遣軍，恭必城守。

translations.literal: Further asked plan of Yin; Yin said: 'South and north together raise—yet Jingzhou has not arrived—if court dispatches troops—Gong necessarily walls and guards.'
translations.idiomatic: He asked Che Yin, who replied, 'North and south rise together but Jingzhou is late—if the court sends troops Wang Gong will fortify.'

sentences.zh: 昔桓公圍壽陽，彌時乃克。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Huan besieged Shouyang—full season then conquered.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Huan once besieged Shouyang for ages before taking it.

sentences.zh: 若京城未拔，而上流奄至，君將何以待之？

translations.literal: If capital city not yet taken—and upper flow suddenly arrives—you, lord, will with what await it?'
translations.idiomatic: If the capital holds while upstream armies strike, how will you answer?'

sentences.zh: 」國寶尤懼，遂上疏解職，詣闕待罪。

translations.literal: Guobao especially feared; thereupon submitted memorial explaining release from office; went to palace gate awaiting crime.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao was terrified, memorialized his resignation, and waited at the palace gate for punishment.'

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，祚稱詔復其本官，欲收其兵距王恭。

translations.literal: Presently regretted it—[someone] throne-called edict restored his original office—wished gather his troops resist Wang Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He regretted it, forged an edict restoring his post, and mustered troops to resist Wang Gong (the character in the text may be a variant of 'forge').

sentences.zh: 道子既不能距諸侯，欲委罪國寶，乃遣譙王尚之收國寶，付廷尉，賜死，並斬緒於市。

translations.literal: Daozi being unable to resist the feudal lords—wished cast blame on Guobao—thereupon sent Prince of Qiao Shangzhi seize Guobao—delivered to commandant—ordered suicide—and together beheaded Xu in market.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to face the provinces, Daozi scapegoated Guobao: Prince Sima Shangzhi arrested him, the commandant ordered suicide, and Wang Xu died in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 以謝王恭。

translations.literal: Thereby apologize to Wang Gong.
translations.idiomatic: This was meant to appease Wang Gong.

sentences.zh: 國寶貪縱聚斂，不知紀極，後房伎妾以百數，天下珍玩充滿其室。

translations.literal: Guobao greedy and unrestrained gathered levies—not knowing limit or extreme—rear chambers singing-girls and concubines by hundreds counted—realm's treasures filled his chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Guobao extorted without limit and kept hundreds of entertainers; rare treasures jammed his halls.

sentences.zh: 及王恭伏法，詔追復國寶本官。

translations.literal: When Wang Gong submitted to law—edict pursued restoring Guobao's original office.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Gong's execution an edict posthumously restored Guobao's titles.

sentences.zh: 元興初，桓玄得志，表徙其家屬于交州。

translations.literal: At beginning of Yuanxing, when Huan Xuan obtained his aim—memorialized shifting his family dependents to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanxing, once Huan Xuan triumphed, he memorialized to exile Guobao's kin to Jiaozhou.

translations.literal: Equals sign (continuity marker in source text).

sentences.zh: 國寶弟忱

translations.literal: Guobao's younger brother Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen (younger brother of Wang Guobao)

sentences.zh: =忱字元達。

translations.literal: = Chen's style name was Yuanda.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen, courtesy name Yuanda,

sentences.zh: 弱冠知名，與王恭、王珣俱流譽一時。

translations.literal: At capping age became known—with Wang Gong, Wang Xun together flowing praise one season.
translations.idiomatic: Celebrated at his capping alongside Wang Gong and Wang Xun.

sentences.zh: 歷位驃騎長史。

translations.literal: Passed through posts chief clerk to agile cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk to the commander of agile cavalry.

sentences.zh: 嘗造其舅范寧，與張玄相遇，寧使與玄語。

translations.literal: Once visited his maternal uncle Fan Ning—with Zhang Xuan encountered—Ning ordered him converse with Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Visiting his uncle Fan Ning he met Zhang Xuan; Fan asked them to talk.

sentences.zh: 玄正坐斂衽，待其有發，忱竟不與言，玄失望便去。

translations.literal: Xuan straight sat gathered lapels—waited for him to have utterance—Chen ultimately did not speak with him—Xuan disappointed then left.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang sat formally waiting for Wang Chen to speak; Wang Chen stayed silent, so Zhang left disappointed.

sentences.zh: 寧讓忱曰：「張玄，吳中之秀，何不與語？

translations.literal: Ning reproached Chen, saying: 'Zhang Xuan—Wu centre's excellence—why not converse with him?'
translations.idiomatic: Fan scolded him: 'Zhang Xuan is Wu's finest scholar—why refuse speech?'

sentences.zh: 」忱笑曰：「張祖希欲相識，自可見詣。

translations.literal: Chen smiled, saying: 'Zhang Zuxi if wishes mutual knowing—may himself come visit.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen smiled: 'If Zhang Zuoxi wants acquaintance, let him call on me.'

sentences.zh: 」寧謂曰：「卿風流雋望，真後來之秀。

translations.literal: Ning told him, saying: 'You wind-flow handsome expectation—truly later-coming's excellence.'
translations.idiomatic: Fan said, 'Your grace marks you among the rising elite.'

sentences.zh: 」忱曰：「不有此舅，焉有此甥！

translations.literal: Chen said: 'Without this uncle—how have this nephew!'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen replied, 'Without such an uncle, how such a nephew!'

sentences.zh: 」既而寧使報玄，玄束帶造之，始為賓主。

translations.literal: Presently Ning sent report Xuan—Xuan bound belt visited him—only then became guest and host.
translations.idiomatic: Fan told Zhang, who belted his robes and paid a formal visit—they then conversed as host and guest.'

sentences.zh: 太元中，出為荊州刺史、都督荊益寧三州軍事、建武將軍、假節。

translations.literal: Within Taiyuan—went out as inspector of Jingzhou—area commander Jing, Yi, Ning three prefectures' military affairs—general who establishes martial—borrowed insignia.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiyuan he became inspector of Jingzhou, commander of Jing, Yi, and Ning forces, general who establishes might, with ceremonial credentials.

sentences.zh: 忱自恃才氣，放酒誕節，慕王澄之為人，又年少居方伯之任，談者憂之。

translations.literal: Chen relied on talent and spirit—released wine and unrestrained restraint—admired Wang Cheng's conduct—further young dwelt regional lord's duty—talkers worried him.
translations.idiomatic: Confident and wilful, he drank wildly and emulated Wang Cheng's eccentric style; observers worried about so young a governor.

sentences.zh: 及鎮荊州，威風肅然，殊得物和。

translations.literal: When garrisoned Jingzhou—awe wind austere—especially obtained things harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Yet ruling Jingzhou he commanded respect and harmony.

sentences.zh: 桓玄時在江陵，既其本國。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan at the time was at Jiangling—already his root state.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was at Jiangling in his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 且奕葉故義，常以才雄駕物。

translations.literal: Further successive-leaves old righteousness—constantly by talent hero rides things.
translations.idiomatic: Generations of ties made Huan Xuan habitually domineering.

sentences.zh: 忱每裁抑之。

translations.literal: Chen often trimmed and restrained him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen repeatedly checked him.

sentences.zh: 玄嘗詣忱，通人未出，乘轝直進。

translations.literal: Xuan once visited Chen—usher not yet out—rode sedan straight entered.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huan Xuan called before the usher appeared and barged in by sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 忱對玄鞭門幹，玄怒，去之，忱亦不留。

translations.literal: Chen toward Xuan whipped gate clerks—Xuan angry—left him—Chen also did not detain.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chen had gate guards whipped in his presence; Huan stormed off and Wang Chen did not detain him.

sentences.zh: 嘗朔日見客，仗衛甚盛，玄言欲獵，借數百人，忱悉給之。

translations.literal: Once new-moon day saw guests—arms guard very grand—Xuan said wished hunt—borrow several hundred persons—Chen entirely supplied them.
translations.idiomatic: On a court day Wang Chen received guests with full guard; Huan asked for hundreds of men for a hunt and Wang Chen supplied them.

sentences.zh: 玄憚而服焉。

translations.literal: Xuan feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan respected him thereafter.

sentences.zh: 性任達不拘，末年尤嗜酒，一飲連月不醒，或裸體而遊，每歡三日不歎，便覺形神不相親。

translations.literal: By nature unrestrained and reaching—not bound—late years especially addicted wine—one drinking successive months not sober—or naked body and roamed—each joy three days not sigh—then felt body and spirit not mutually intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Wild and unrestrained, in old age he drank for months on end, sometimes wandered naked; prolonged revel left body and soul estranged.

sentences.zh: 婦父嘗有慘，忱乘醉吊之，婦父慟哭，忱與賓客十許人，連臂被髮裸身而入，繞之三幣百而出。

translations.literal: Wife's father once had grief—Chen rode drunk condoled—wife's father wailed—Chen with guests ten and more—linked arms draped hair naked body entered—circled it three coins hundred exited.
translations.idiomatic: When his father-in-law mourned, Wang Chen arrived drunk; while the elder wept, Wang Chen and a dozen guests linked arms, hair loose and naked, entered and circled the bier three times before leaving (text defective at end).

sentences.zh: 其所行多此類。

translations.literal: What he practised—much this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Much of his conduct matched this excess.

sentences.zh: 數年卒官，追贈右將軍，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Several years died in office—posthumously awarded general of the right—posthumous title said Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office after a few years and was posthumously named general of the right with epithet Mu.

translations.literal: Equals sign (continuity marker in source text).

sentences.zh: 愉子綏

translations.literal: Yu's son Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui (son of Wang Yu)

sentences.zh: =綏字彥猷。

translations.literal: = Sui's style name was Yanyou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui, courtesy name Yanyou,

sentences.zh: 少有美稱，厚自矜邁，實鄙而無行。

translations.literal: In youth had fair praise—thick self-pride stride—actually base and without conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Praised in youth yet arrogant—mean-spirited beneath the polish.

sentences.zh: 愉為殷、桓所捕，綏未測存亡，在都有憂色，居處飲食，每事貶降，時人每謂為「試守孝子」。

translations.literal: Yu was by Yin, Huan seized—Sui not yet fathomed survival death—in capital had anxious colour—dwelling eating drinking—each affair lowered reduced—men of time often called him 'probation guarding filial son.'
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yu fell into Yin and Huan's hands, Wang Sui—unsure if his father lived—feigned mourning so shallowly that people mocked him as a 'trial-period filial son.'

sentences.zh: 桓玄之為太尉，綏以桓氏甥甚見寵待，為太尉右長史。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan became grand commandant—Sui because Huan clan nephew greatly seen favoured treated—became grand commandant right chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan served as grand commandant he favoured his nephew Wang Sui as senior clerk.

sentences.zh: 及玄篡，遷中書令。

translations.literal: When Xuan usurped—transferred director of palace writers.
translations.idiomatic: After the usurpation Wang Sui became director of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 劉裕建義，以為冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When Liu Yu established righteousness—appointed champion general.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu raised the loyal army Wang Sui was named champion general.

sentences.zh: 其家夜中梁上無故有人頭墮於床，而流血滂沲。

translations.literal: His household at night on beam without cause someone's head fell on bed—and flowing blood vast.
translations.idiomatic: A severed head dropped from a beam onto his bed in a shower of blood.

sentences.zh: 俄拜荊州刺史、假節。

translations.literal: Soon appointed inspector of Jingzhou—borrowed insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named inspector of Jingzhou with credentials.

sentences.zh: 坐父愉之謀，與弟納並被誅。

translations.literal: Sat father's Yu's plot—with younger brother Na together were executed.
translations.idiomatic: His father's plot implicated him and his brother Wang Na—both were executed.

sentences.zh: 初，綏與王謐、桓胤齊名，為後進之秀。

translations.literal: Formerly Sui with Wang Mi, Huan Yin equal name—were rear-progress's excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Sui ranked with Wang Mi and Huan Yin among rising talents.

sentences.zh: 謐位官既極，保身而終。

translations.literal: Mi position office already extreme—preserved body and ended.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi rose to the top yet survived.

sentences.zh: 胤以從坐誅，聲稱猶全。

translations.literal: Yin because attendant sitting executed—voice praise still whole.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Yin died as an accessory yet kept his reputation.

sentences.zh: 綏身死，名論殆盡，亦以薄行矜峭而尚人故也。

translations.literal: Sui body died—name discussions nearly exhausted—also because thin conduct pride steep and esteem men cause.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui died in disgrace—his shallow swagger had invited it.

sentences.zh: 自昶父漢雁門太守澤已有名稱，忱又秀出，綏亦著稱，八葉繼軌，軒冕莫與為比焉。

translations.literal: From Chang's father Han Yanmen governor Ze already had name designation—Chen further excellence out—Sui also noted praise—eight leaves inherit tracks—carriage caps none with compare.
translations.idiomatic: From Wang Ze of Han down through Wang Chang to Wang Chen and Wang Sui—eight generations of high office unmatched by any clan.

translations.literal: Equals sign (continuity marker in source text).

sentences.zh: 族子嶠

translations.literal: Clan nephew Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiao (clansman)

sentences.zh: =嶠字開山。

translations.literal: = Qiao's style name was Kaishan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiao, courtesy name Kaishan,

sentences.zh: 祖默，魏尚書。

translations.literal: Grandfather Mo—Wei masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Mo served Wei as minister.

sentences.zh: 父佑，以才智稱，為楊駿腹心。

translations.literal: Father You—by talent and wisdom praised—was Yang Jun's belly heart.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang You, famed for ability, was Yang Jun's confidant.

sentences.zh: 駿之排汝南王亮，退衛瓘，皆佑之謀也。

translations.literal: Jun's expelling Prince of Runan Liang—retiring Wei Guan—all were You's plots.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's purge of Prince Sima Liang of Runan and dismissal of Wei Guan were Wang You's schemes.

sentences.zh: 位至北軍中候。

translations.literal: Position reached northern army central inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to inspector of the northern armies.

sentences.zh: 嶠少有風尚，並、司二州交辟，不就。

translations.literal: Qiao in youth had wind and bearing—Bing, Si two prefectures mutually summoned—did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful Wang Qiao won simultaneous summons from Bing and Si—he declined.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，攜其二弟避亂渡江。

translations.literal: Yongjia end—carried his two younger brothers fled turmoil crossed river.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yongjia he fled south with two brothers.

sentences.zh: 時元帝鎮建鄴，教曰：「王佑三息始至，名德之胄，並有操行，宜蒙飾敘。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan-di garrisoned Jianye—instruction said: 'Wang You's three breaths just arrived—name virtue's descendants—together have conduct and practice—ought receive ornament and ordering.'
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Rui ordered rewards for Wang You's three sons—men of pedigree and conduct deserving titles.'

sentences.zh: 且可給錢三十萬，帛三百匹，米五十斛，親兵二十人。

translations.literal: Further may supply cash three hundred thousand—silk three hundred bolts—rice fifty hu—personal guards twenty persons.'
translations.idiomatic: Grant three hundred thousand cash, three hundred bolts of silk, fifty hu of rice, and twenty guards.'

sentences.zh: 」尋以嶠參世子東中郎軍事。

translations.literal: Soon with Qiao participate heir-apparent eastern centre army military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiao was soon named aide on the heir apparent's eastern army staff.'

sentences.zh: 不就。

translations.literal: Did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: He declined.

sentences.zh: 湣帝徵拜著作郎，右丞相南陽王保辟，皆以道險不行。

translations.literal: Min-di summoned appointed editorial director—right chancellor Prince of Nanyang Bao summoned—both because roads perilous did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Min's call to the editorial office and Prince Sima Bao of Nanyang's summons failed—roads were unsafe.

sentences.zh: 元帝作相，以為水曹屬，除長山令，遷太子中舍人以疾不拜。

translations.literal: Yuan-di acted chancellor—appointed water bureau subordinate—appointed Changshan magistrate—transferred heir-apparent centre lodger—because illness did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: As prime minister, Prince Yuan named him to the water bureau, then magistrate of Changshan; he was offered palace aide to the heir apparent but cited illness.

sentences.zh: 王敦請為參軍，爵九原縣公。

translations.literal: Wang Dun requested [him] as army adviser—noble rank Jiuyuan county duke.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun recruited him as military aide with the noble rank Duke of Jiuyuan county.

sentences.zh: 敦在石頭，欲禁私伐蔡洲荻，以問群下。

translations.literal: Dun at Stone Citadel—wished forbid private cutting Cai Isle reeds—thereby asked assembled subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: At Stone Citadel Wang Dun proposed banning private reed-cutting on Cai Isle and polled his staff.

sentences.zh: 時王師新敗，士庶震懼，莫敢異議。

translations.literal: At time royal army newly defeated—gentlemen and commoners trembled and feared—none dared divergent opinion.
translations.idiomatic: After the recent defeat none dared oppose him.

sentences.zh: 嶠獨曰：「中原有菽，庶人采之。

translations.literal: Qiao alone said: 'Central plain has beans—commoners gather them.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiao alone said, 'The Odes sing that common folk may gather beans on common ground.'

sentences.zh: 百姓不足，君孰與足！

translations.literal: Hundred surnames not sufficient—lord with whom sufficient!'
translations.idiomatic: When the people lack enough, what can the ruler have?'

sentences.zh: 若禁人樵伐，未知其可。

translations.literal: If forbid men firewood cutting—not yet know its permissibility.'
translations.idiomatic: Banning fuel gathering may not be wise.'

sentences.zh: 」敦不悅。

translations.literal: Dun was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun took offence.

sentences.zh: 敦將殺周顗、戴若思，嶠於坐諫曰：「濟濟多士，交王以寧。

translations.literal: Dun was about to kill Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi; Qiao at seat remonstrated, saying: 'Multitudes of gentlemen assist the king and bring peace.'
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Dun prepared to execute Zhou Yi and Dai Ruosi, Wang Qiao objected: 'The king needs his ministers—how slaughter noted scholars to save yourself?'

sentences.zh: 安可戮諸名士，以自全生！

translations.literal: How can one slaughter the various famed gentlemen thereby to preserve one's life!'
translations.idiomatic: You cannot butcher eminent scholars merely to survive!'

sentences.zh: 」敦大怒，欲斬嶠，賴謝鯤以免。

translations.literal: Dun greatly raged and wished to behead Qiao—relied on Xie Kun to escape.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun flew into a rage and nearly executed Wang Qiao; Xie Kun saved him.

sentences.zh: 敦猶銜之，出為領軍長史。

translations.literal: Dun still harboured resentment—sent him out as chief clerk to the army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun still nursed a grudge and posted him as chief clerk to the commander of armies.

sentences.zh: 敦平後，除中書侍郎，兼大著作，固辭。

translations.literal: After Dun was pacified—appointed gentleman of the palace writers—concurrently grand editorial director—firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun's defeat Wang Qiao was offered secretary of the palace secretariat and chief compiler—he refused.

sentences.zh: 轉越騎校尉，頻遷吏部郎、御史中丞、秘書監，領本州大中正。

translations.literal: Transferred colonel of fierce cavalry—by stages transferred gentleman of personnel bureau, metropolitan shepherd, overseer of the palace library—headed home prefecture senior rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: He became colonel of fierce cavalry, then personnel secretary, metropolitan shepherd, palace librarian, and senior rectifier for his province.

sentences.zh: 咸和初，朝議欲以嶠為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: At beginning of Xianhe—court deliberation wished to make Qiao governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianhe the court meant to name him governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 嶠以京尹望重，不宜以疾居之，求補廬陵郡，乃拜嶠廬陵太守。

translations.literal: Qiao because capital governor's expectation is heavy—not suitable with illness to dwell in it—requested supplement Luling commandery—thereupon appointed Qiao Luling governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiao argued that the capital governorship was too weighty for an ailing man and asked for Luling—so he became governor of Luling.

sentences.zh: 以嶠家貧，無以上道，賜布百匹。

translations.literal: Because Qiao's household was poor—nothing wherewith to ascend the road—bestowed cloth one hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him a hundred bolts because he could not afford the journey.

sentences.zh: 錢十萬。

translations.literal: Cash one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Plus one hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: Soon died in office—posthumous title said Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office soon after with epithet Mu.

sentences.zh: 子淡嗣，歷位右衛將軍、侍中、中護軍、尚書、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Son Dan succeeded—passed through posts general of the right guard, attendant-in-ordinary, central protector, masters of writing, inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wang Dan inherited his rank and rose to Right Guard commander, attendant-in-ordinary, central protector, minister, and inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 淡子度世，驍騎將軍。

translations.literal: Dan's son Dushi—general of nimble cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dushi became general of nimble cavalry.

sentences.zh: 袁悅之

translations.literal: Yuan Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yuezhi

sentences.zh: 袁悅之，字元禮，陳郡陽夏人也。

translations.literal: Yuan Yuezhi—style name Yuanli—was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yuezhi, courtesy name Yuanli, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 父朗，給事中。

translations.literal: Father Lang—palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan Lang served as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 悅之能長短說，甚有精理。

translations.literal: Yuezhi could long-and-short persuasion—had very subtle principle.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at sophistry with acute reasoning.

sentences.zh: 始為謝玄參軍，為玄所遇，丁憂去職。

translations.literal: First was Xie Xuan's army adviser—was favoured by Xuan—ding mourning left office.
translations.idiomatic: He began as military aide to Xie Xuan, earned favour, then resigned for mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋還都，止齎《戰國策》，言天下要惟此書。

translations.literal: When mourning ended returned capital—only carried Warring States Stratagems—said world's essentials only this book.
translations.idiomatic: Returning after mourning he carried only the Warring States Stratagems, claiming it held the keys to power.

sentences.zh: 後甚為會稽王道子所親愛，每勸道子專覽朝權，道子頗納其說。

translations.literal: Later greatly by Prince of Guiji Daozi was beloved—often urged Daozi monopolize viewing court power—Daozi rather adopted his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daozi of Guiji grew fond of him; Yuan urged Daozi to monopolize court power and Daozi listened.

sentences.zh: 俄而見誅。

translations.literal: Soon was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon executed.

translations.literal: Equals sign (continuity marker in source text).

sentences.zh: 祖台之

translations.literal: Zu Taizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Taizhi

sentences.zh: =祖-{台}-之，字元辰，范陽人也。

translations.literal: = Zu Taizhi—style name Yuanchen—was a man of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Taizhi, courtesy name Yuanchen, came from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 官至侍中、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Office reached attendant-in-ordinary, grand master of splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant-in-ordinary and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 撰《志怪》，書行於世。

translations.literal: Composed Records of the Strange—book circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Records of the Strange, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 荀崧

translations.literal: Xun Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Song

sentences.zh: 荀崧，字景猷，潁川臨潁人，魏太尉彧之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Xun Song—style name Jingyou—was a man of Linlei in Yingchuan—great-grandson of Wei grand commandant Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Song, courtesy name Jingyou, from Linlei in Yingchuan, was great-grandson of the Wei grand commandant Xun Yu.

sentences.zh: 父頵，羽林右監、安陵鄉侯，與王濟、何劭為拜親之友。

translations.literal: Father Yi—right inspector of the feathered forest, village marquis of Anling—with Wang Ji, He Shao were bowing-kin friends.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun Yi commanded the guards and held the village marquisate of Anling; he was sworn kin to Wang Ji and He Shao.

sentences.zh: 崧志操清純，雅好文學。

translations.literal: Song's aspiration and conduct pure—refined love of literature.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Song's character was pure and he loved letters.

sentences.zh: 齠齔時，族曾祖顗見而奇之，以為必興頵門。

translations.literal: When shedding milk-teeth—clan great-grandfather Yi saw and marvelled—thought would surely raise Yi's gate.
translations.idiomatic: While still a child his kinsman Xun Yi foresaw he would revive the clan.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，太原王濟甚相器重，以方其外祖陳郡袁侃，謂侃弟奧曰：「近見荀監子，清虛名理，當不及父，德性純粹，是賢兄輩人也。

translations.literal: At capping—Taiyuan Wang Ji greatly esteemed him—compared with his maternal grandfather Yuan Kan of Chen command—said to Kan's younger brother Ao: 'Recently saw Inspector Xun's son—clear empty name principle—perhaps not reaching father—virtue nature pure—this is worthy elder-brother generation person.'
translations.idiomatic: At his capping Wang Ji of Taiyuan admired him and likened him to his maternal grandfather Yuan Kan, telling Yuan Ao, 'The boy rivals his father in doctrine but matches your brothers in sheer virtue.'

sentences.zh: 」其為名流所賞如此。

translations.literal: Thus was he prized by the eminent.
translations.idiomatic: Leading figures esteemed him thus.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，詔以崧代兄襲父爵，補濮陽王允文學。

translations.literal: Within Taishi—edict ordered Song replace elder brother inherit father's noble rank—supplemented Prince of Puyang Yun literary scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taishi an edict let him inherit his father's title in place of his brother and tutor Prince Yun of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 與王敦、顧榮、陸機等友善，趙王倫引為相國參軍。

translations.literal: With Wang Dun, Gu Rong, Lu Ji etc. friendly—Prince of Zhao Lun summoned as chancellor's army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: Friends with Wang Dun, Gu Rong, and Lu Ji, he joined Prince Sima Lun as military aide.

sentences.zh: 倫篡，轉護軍司馬、給事中，稍遷尚書吏部郎、太弟中庶子，累遷侍中、中護軍。

translations.literal: When Lun usurped—transferred marshal of the guards—palace attendant—gradually gentleman of personnel—heir-apparent's eastern palace attendant—by stages attendant-in-ordinary, central protector.
translations.idiomatic: After the usurpation he rose through marshal of guards, palace aide, personnel secretary, attendant to the heir apparent, attendant-in-ordinary, and central protector.

sentences.zh: 王彌入洛，崧與百官奔於密，未至而母亡。

translations.literal: When Wang Mi entered Luoyang—Song with hundred officials fled toward Mi—not arrived yet mother died.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mi took Luoyang, Xun Song fled toward Mi with the court but his mother died en route.

sentences.zh: 賊追將及，同旅散走，崧被髮從車，守喪號泣。

translations.literal: Bandits pursued about to reach—travelling companions scattered fled—Song draped hair followed cart—guarding mourning wailed wept.
translations.idiomatic: As bandits closed in his companions fled; Xun Song loosed his hair, rode with his mother's bier, and wailed.

sentences.zh: 賊至，棄其母屍於地，奪車而去。

translations.literal: Bandits arrived—cast aside his mother's corpse on ground—seized cart and left.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders threw down the corpse and stole his cart.

sentences.zh: 崧被四創，氣絕，至夜方蘇。

translations.literal: Song received four wounds—breath cut—until night then revived.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Song suffered four cuts and lay senseless until night.

sentences.zh: 葬母於密山。

translations.literal: Buried mother on Mi mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He buried her on Mount Mi.

sentences.zh: 服闋，族父籓承制，以崧監江北軍事、南中郎將、後將軍、假節、襄城太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended—clan father Fan acting authority—appointed Song supervise Jiangbei military affairs—general of the southern centre—general of the rear—borrowed insignia—Xiangcheng governor.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his kinsman Sima Fan, acting under orders, put him in charge of Jiangbei forces as general of the southern centre and rear with credentials and as governor of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 時山陵發掘，崧遣主簿石覽將兵入洛，修復山陵。

translations.literal: At time imperial tombs dug up—Song sent chief clerk Shi Lan lead troops enter Luoyang—repair imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang tombs were looted he sent Shi Lan to restore them.

sentences.zh: 以勳進爵舞陽縣公，遷都督荊州江北諸軍事、平南將軍，鎮宛，改封曲陵公。

translations.literal: By merit advanced noble rank Wuyang county duke—transferred area commander Jingzhou Jiangbei military affairs—general who pacifies south—garrisoned Wan—changed enfeoffment Quling duke.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he became Duke of Wuyang county, commander of Jingzhou north-of-the-Yangzi forces, general who pacifies the south at Wan, later retitled Duke of Quling.

sentences.zh: 為賊杜曾所圍。

translations.literal: Was by bandit Du Zeng besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit Du Zeng besieged him.

sentences.zh: 石覽時為襄城太守，崧力弱食盡，使其小女灌求救于覽及南中郎將周訪。

translations.literal: Shi Lan at time was Xiangcheng governor—Song strength weak food exhausted—ordered his young daughter Guan seek rescue from Lan and general of southern centre Zhou Fang.
translations.idiomatic: With grain gone Xun Song sent his daughter Xun Guan through the lines to Shi Lan and Zhou Fang.

sentences.zh: 訪即遣子撫率兵三千人會石覽，俱救崧。

translations.literal: Fang immediately sent son Fu lead troops three thousand persons join Shi Lan—together rescued Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fang sent Zhou Fu with three thousand men alongside Shi Lan to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 賊聞兵至，散走。

translations.literal: Bandits heard troops arrived—scattered fled.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng's men fled at their approach.

sentences.zh: 崧既得免，乃遣南陽中部尉王國、劉願等潛軍襲穰縣，獲曾從兄偽新野太守保，斬之。

translations.literal: Song having obtained escape—thereupon sent Nanyang central division captain Wang Guo, Liu Yuan etc. stealth army raid Rang county—captured Zeng's cousin false Xinye governor Bao—beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Once free he ambushed Rang, seized Du Zeng's kinsman Bao who posed as Xinye governor, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 元帝踐阼，徵拜尚書僕射，使崧與協共定中興禮儀。

translations.literal: Yuan-di ascended throne—summoned superintendent of masters of writing—ordered Song with Xie together settle restoration ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan summoned him as vice-director of the masters of writing to codify court ritual with Diao Xie.

sentences.zh: 從弟馗早亡，二息序、廞，年各數歲，崧迎與共居，恩同其子。

translations.literal: Younger clan cousin Kui early died—two sons Xu, Yin—years each several ages—Song welcomed together dwelt—grace same as his sons.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his cousin's young sons Xu and Yin as his own.

sentences.zh: 太尉、臨淮公荀顗國胤廢絕，朝庭以崧屬近，欲以崧子襲封。

translations.literal: Grand commandant—Duke of Linhuai Xun Yi state heir cut off—court because Song kinship near—wished Song's son inherit enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun Yi's line ended the court meant for Xun Song's son to inherit the ducal title.

sentences.zh: 崧哀序孤微，乃讓封與序，論者稱焉。

translations.literal: Song pitied Xu's orphan lowliness—thereupon yielded enfeoffment to Xu—discussants praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying orphan Xu he yielded the title—critics praised him.

sentences.zh: 轉太常。

translations.literal: Transferred chamberlain of ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He became chamberlain of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時方修學校，簡省博士，置《周易》王氏、《尚書》鄭氏、《古文尚書》孔氏、《毛詩》鄭氏、《周官禮記》鄭氏、《春秋左傳》杜氏服氏、《論語》《孝經》鄭氏博士各一人，凡九人，其《儀禮》、《公羊》、《穀梁》及鄭《易》皆省不置。

translations.literal: At time just repairing schools—selected reduced erudites—placed Zhou yi Wang, Documents Zheng, old-text Documents Kong, Mao Odes Zheng, Zhou offices Rites Zheng, Zuo commentary Du and Fu, Analects Filial Piety Zheng erudites each one person—total nine persons—the Ceremonies, Gongyang, Guliang and Zheng Changes all reduced not placed.
translations.idiomatic: While refurbishing the academy the court named nine royal doctoral chairs—for Wang's Zhou yi, Zheng's Documents, Kong's old-text Documents, Zheng's Mao Odes and Rites, Du's and Fu's Zuo, and Zheng's Analects and Filial Piety—and dropped the Ceremonies, Gongyang, Guliang, and Zheng's Changes.

sentences.zh: 崧以為不可，乃上疏曰：

translations.literal: Song thought not permissible—thereupon submitted memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xun Song disagreed and memorialized:

sentences.zh: 元帝詔曰：「崧表如此，皆經國之務。

translations.literal: Yuan-di edict said: 'Song's memorial thus—all are binding state's tasks.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan replied, 'Xun Song speaks to the state's essentials.'

sentences.zh: 為政所由。

translations.literal: They are the foundation from which governance proceeds.
translations.idiomatic: They chart the foundations of sound rule.

sentences.zh: 息馬投戈，猶可講藝，今雖日不暇給，豈忘本而遺存邪！

translations.literal: Rest horses cast aside spears—still can lecture arts—now although days lack leisure to supply—how forget root and abandon preservation!'
translations.idiomatic: Even after arms we must teach the classics—busy though we are we cannot abandon roots!'

sentences.zh: 可共博議者詳之。

translations.literal: May together broadly deliberate examine them.'
translations.idiomatic: Let ministers debate them.'

sentences.zh: 」議者多請從崧所奏。

translations.literal: Deliberators many requested follow Song's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Most advisers sided with Xun Song.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「《穀梁》膚淺，不足置博士，余如奏。

translations.literal: Edict said: 'Guliang superficial—not sufficient place erudite—the rest like memorial.'
translations.idiomatic: The edict kept only Guliang omitted; the rest followed his plea.'

sentences.zh: 」會王敦之難，不行。

translations.literal: It happened Wang Dun's turmoil—not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun's rebellion prevented implementation.'

sentences.zh: 敦表以崧為尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Dun memorialized appoint Song masters of writing left superintendent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun named him left vice-director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，群臣議廟號，王敦遣使謂曰：「豺狼當路，梓宮未反，祖宗之號，宜別思詳。

translations.literal: When emperor died—assembled ministers deliberated temple title—Wang Dun sent envoy telling them: 'Jackals and wolves block road—cypress palace not returned—ancestors' titles—ought separately think carefully.'
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan's death Wang Dun's envoy urged delaying the temple name while dangers lingered.'

sentences.zh: 」崧議以為：「禮，祖有功，宗有德。

translations.literal: Song deliberated thinking: 'Rite—ancestor has merit—exemplar has virtue.'
translations.idiomatic: Xun Song cited ritual: ancestors earn the title Zu when meritorious.'

sentences.zh: 元皇帝天縱聖哲，光啟中興，德澤侔於太戊，功惠邁于漢宣，臣敢依前典，上號曰中宗。

translations.literal: Yuan emperor Heaven-abandon sage wisdom—light opens restoration—virtue dew matches Taewu—merit kindness surpasses Han Xuan—your subject dares rely prior canons—offer title called Zhongzong.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan Heaven-sent sage whose virtue matched Taewu and feats surpassed Han Xuandi—I propose Zhongzong.'

sentences.zh: 」既而與敦書曰：「承以長蛇未翦，別詳祖宗。

translations.literal: Presently with Dun wrote saying: 'Received because long snake not cut—separately deliberate ancestors.'
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Wang Dun: 'You cite unrest to postpone the temple debate.'

sentences.zh: 先帝應天受命，以隆中興；

translations.literal: Late emperor responded Heaven received mandate—thereby elevate restoration.'
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor received Heaven's mandate to revive Jin.'

sentences.zh: 中興之主，寧可隨世數而遷毀！

translations.literal: Restoration's lord—how can follow generations and shift ruin!'
translations.idiomatic: Such a founder cannot wait on petty chronology!'

sentences.zh: 敢率丹直。

translations.literal: Dare lead cinnabar straight.'
translations.idiomatic: I speak plainly.'

sentences.zh: 詢之朝野，上號中宗。

translations.literal: Inquired court and wild—offered title Zhongzong.'
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside agree on Zhongzong.'

sentences.zh: 卜日有期，不及重請，專輒之愆，所不敢辭。

translations.literal: Divining day has term—not reaching repeat request—special presumption's fault—not dare decline.'
translations.idiomatic: The rites were scheduled—I could not await another petition though that risks offence.'

sentences.zh: 」初，敦待崧甚厚，欲以為司空，於此銜之而止。

translations.literal: Formerly Dun treated Song very thick—wished make minister of works—at this harboured resentment and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun had meant to make him minister of works—this letter ended that.

sentences.zh: 太寧初，加散騎常侍，後領太子太傅。

translations.literal: Taiping beginning—added attendant at large and regular attendant—later headed heir-apparent grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taiping he became imperial attendant and later grand tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 以平王敦功，更封平樂伯。

translations.literal: By pacifying Wang Dun merit—further enfeoffment Pingyue earl.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Wang Dun he received the earldom of Pingyue.

sentences.zh: 坐使威儀為猛獸所食，免職。

translations.literal: Sat crime attendants ritual by fierce beasts eaten—removed office.
translations.idiomatic: His ceremonial guards were devoured by a beast—he lost office.

sentences.zh: 後拜金紫光祿大夫、錄尚書事，散騎常侍如故。

translations.literal: Later appointed golden purple grand master of splendid happiness—recording masters of writing affairs—attendant at large as before.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became golden-purple grand master and overseer of the masters of writing while keeping his attendant post.

sentences.zh: 遷右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，錄尚書如故。

translations.literal: Transferred right splendid happiness grand master—establish headquarters parity with Three Excellencies—recording masters of writing as before.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right grand master with independent headquarters and kept recording duties.

sentences.zh: 又領秘書監，給親兵百二十人。

translations.literal: Further headed palace library—given personal guards one hundred twenty persons.
translations.idiomatic: He also directed the palace library with a guard of one hundred twenty.

sentences.zh: 年雖衰老，而孜孜典籍，世以此嘉之。

translations.literal: Years although decay old—yet diligent diligent classics—age on this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Age did not dull his devotion to books—admired by all.

sentences.zh: 蘇峻之役，崧與王導、陸曄共登御床擁衛帝，及帝被逼幸石頭，崧亦侍從不離帝側。

translations.literal: Su Jun's campaign—Song with Wang Dao, Lu Ye together ascended imperial couch embracing guarding emperor—when emperor forced fortunate Stone Citadel—Song also attended followed not leave emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun's coup he mounted the imperial couch with Wang Dao and Lu Ye to shield the emperor and stayed at his side in Stone Citadel.

sentences.zh: 賊平，帝幸溫嶠舟，崧時年老病篤，猶力步而從。

translations.literal: Bandits pacified—emperor fortunate Wen Qiao's boat—Song at time aged sick severe—still forced walked followed.
translations.idiomatic: After victory he followed Emperor Ming to Wen Qiao's boat though aged and ill.

sentences.zh: 薨，時年六十七。

translations.literal: Died—at time age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: Posthumously attendant-in-ordinary—posthumous title said Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named attendant-in-ordinary with epithet Jing.

sentences.zh: 其後著作郎虞預與丞相王導箋曰：「伏見前秘書、光祿大夫荀公，生於積德之族，少有儒雅之稱，歷位內外，在貴能降。

translations.literal: Afterwards editorial director Yu Yu with chancellor Wang Dao note said: 'Prostrate see former palace secretary—splendid grand master Lord Xun—born in accumulated virtue clan—in youth had refined Ru praise—passed posts inner outer—in noble able descend.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yu later wrote Wang Dao praising Xun Song's pedigree, scholarship, and humility.'

sentences.zh: 蘇峻肆虐，乘輿失幸，公處嫌忌之地，有累卵之危，朝士為之寒心，論者謂之不免。

translations.literal: Su Jun violent cruelty—imperial carriage lost favour—lord dwelt suspicious jealous ground—had piled eggs peril—court gentlemen for it chilled heart—discussers called him not spared.
translations.idiomatic: During Su Jun's terror he stood on eggshells yet critics expected him to fall.'

sentences.zh: 而公將之以智，險而不懾，扶侍至尊，繾綣不離。

translations.literal: Yet lord led them with wisdom—peril yet not fear—supported attended supreme—intimate not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he guided with wit, faced peril undaunted, and never left the sovereign.'

sentences.zh: 雖無扶迎之勳，宜蒙守節之報。

translations.literal: Although without supporting welcome merit—ought receive guarding integrity reward.
translations.idiomatic: Though lacking escort feats he deserves reward for steadfast loyalty.'

sentences.zh: 且其宣慈之美，早彰遠近，朝野之望，許以台司，雖未正位，已加儀同。

translations.literal: Further his proclaiming kindness's beauty—early displayed far near—court wild's expectation—promised Three Offices—although not rectified position—already added ceremonies parity.
translations.idiomatic: His kindness was famed; court and countryside marked him for the Three Dukes—ceremony already matched though rank lagged.'

sentences.zh: 至守終純固，名定闔棺，而薨卒之日，直加侍中。

translations.literal: As to guarding end pure firm—name settled closing coffin—yet dying day's end—only added attendant-in-ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He died stainless yet gained only attendant-in-ordinary.'

sentences.zh: 生有三槐之望，沒無鼎足之名，寵不增於前秩，榮不副於本望，此一時愚智所慷慨也。

translations.literal: Living had three locusts' expectation—dying lacked tripod-foot name—favour not increased from prior rank—glory not match original expectation—this one moment fool wise alike stirring.
translations.idiomatic: Honoured in life yet slighted in death—every observer protested.'

sentences.zh: 今承大弊之後，淳風頹散，苟有一介之善，宜在旌表之例，而況國之元老，志節若斯者乎！

translations.literal: Now inheriting great decay after—pure wind ruined scattered—if have one bundle's good—ought be within banner commendation cases—moreover state's elder prime—will integrity like this!'
translations.idiomatic: After disaster even small merits deserve honour—how much more an elder statesman of such fibre!'

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: Not followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court refused.'

sentences.zh: ，崧改葬，詔賜錢百萬，布五千匹。

translations.literal: [Fragment:] —Song reburied—edict bestowed cash million—cloth five thousand bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Xun Song was reburied, an edict granted one million cash and five thousand bolts.

sentences.zh: 有二子：蕤、羨。

translations.literal: Had two sons: Rui, Xian.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xun Rui and Xun Xian.

sentences.zh: 蕤嗣。

translations.literal: Rui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Rui inherited.

translations.literal: Equals sign (continuity marker in source text).

sentences.zh: 子蕤

translations.literal: Son Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Rui (his son)

sentences.zh: =蕤字令遠。

translations.literal: = Rui's style name was Lingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Rui, courtesy name Lingyuan,

sentences.zh: 起家秘書郎，稍遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Raised from home palace secretary gentleman—gradually transferred masters of writing left aide.
translations.idiomatic: He began as palace secretary and rose to left aide in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 蕤有儀操風望，雅為簡文帝所重。

translations.literal: Rui had deportment and bearing wind expectation—refinedly by Emperor Jianwen was esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: His dignity won Emperor Jianwen's respect.

sentences.zh: 時桓溫平蜀，朝廷欲以豫章郡封溫。

translations.literal: At the time Huan Wen pacified Shu—court wished to enfeoff Wen with Yuzhang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Wen conquered Shu the court meant to grant him Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 蕤言於帝曰：「若溫復假王威，北平河洛，修復園陵，將何以加此！

translations.literal: Rui spoke to emperor saying: 'If Wen again borrows kingly awe—north pacifies He-Luo—repairs imperial tombs—what reward can surpass this!'
translations.idiomatic: Xun Rui told the emperor, 'If Huan Wen uses royal prestige to recover the north and restore the tombs, no title tops that.'

sentences.zh: 」於是乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The enfeoffment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 轉散騎常侍、少府，不拜，出補東陽太守。

translations.literal: Transferred attendant at large and regular attendant, junior steward—did not accept—went out supplemented Dongyang governor.
translations.idiomatic: He was offered attendant and junior steward, declined, and became governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 除建威將軍、吳國內史。

translations.literal: Appointed general who establishes might, interior minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He received the titles general who establishes might and interior minister of Wu.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: Died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 籍嗣位，至散騎常侍、大長秋。

translations.literal: Ji succeeded position—reached attendant at large, grand prolonger of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun Ji inherited and rose to attendant at large and grand prolonger of autumn.

translations.literal: Equals sign (continuity marker in source text).

sentences.zh: 蕤第羨

translations.literal: Rui's younger brother Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xian (younger brother of Xun Rui)

sentences.zh: =羨字令則。

translations.literal: = Xian's style name was Lingze.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xian, courtesy name Lingze,

sentences.zh: 清和有准。

translations.literal: Clear and harmonious with measure.
translations.idiomatic: Serene and even-tempered.

sentences.zh: 才年七歲，遇蘇峻難，隨父在石頭，峻甚愛之，恆置膝上。

translations.literal: Only age seven—met Su Jun turmoil—followed father at Stone Citadel—Jun greatly loved him—always placed on knees.
translations.idiomatic: At seven during Su Jun's coup he stayed with his father in Stone Citadel; Su Jun doted on him and kept him on his lap.

sentences.zh: 羨陰白其母，曰：「得一利刀子，足以殺賊。

translations.literal: Xian secretly told his mother, saying: 'Obtain one sharp knife—sufficient to kill bandits.'
translations.idiomatic: He whispered to his mother that a sharp knife would let him kill the rebel.

sentences.zh: 」母掩其口，曰：「無妄言！

translations.literal: Mother covered his mouth, saying: 'Do not reckless speak!'
translations.idiomatic: His mother clapped a hand over his mouth and hushed him.'

sentences.zh: 」年十五，將尚尋陽公主，羨不欲連婚帝室，仍遠遁去。

translations.literal: Age fifteen—about to marry Princess of Xunyang—Xian did not wish connect marriage imperial house—thereupon fled far away.
translations.idiomatic: Betrothed to the Princess of Xunyang at fifteen, he fled rather than marry into the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 監司追，不獲已，乃出尚公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: Inspector pursued—not obtained already—thereupon came out and married princess—appointed consort commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Officials ran him down; forced to comply he married and became consort commandant.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，與琅邪王洽齊名，沛國劉惔、太原王濛、陳郡殷浩並與交好。

translations.literal: At capping—with Langye Wang Qia equal name—Pei Liu Tan, Taiyuan Wang Meng, Chen Yin Hao together befriended.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he ranked with Wang Qia of Langye and enjoyed Liu Tan, Wang Meng, and Yin Hao.

sentences.zh: 驃騎將軍何充出鎮京口，請為參軍。

translations.literal: General of agile cavalry He Chong went out garrisoned Jingkou—requested him as army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong, general of agile cavalry, asked him to serve as military aide at Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 穆帝又以為撫軍參軍，征補太常博士，皆不就。

translations.literal: Emperor Mu again appointed army adviser to the general who pacifies the army—summoned supplemental grand chamberlain erudite—all did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mu named him aide on the pacification staff and offered a doctorate—he refused both.

sentences.zh: 後拜秘書丞、義興太守。

translations.literal: Later appointed assistant director of the palace library, governor of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He later became assistant palace librarian and governor of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 征北將軍褚裒以為長史。

translations.literal: General who conquers the north Chu Ai took him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Ai, general who conquers the north, made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 既到，裒謂佐吏曰：「荀生資逸群之氣，將有沖天之舉，諸君宜善事之。

translations.literal: Having arrived—Ai told assistant clerks saying: 'Mr Xun bears transcendent qi—will have heaven-soaring deed—you gentlemen ought serve him well.'
translations.idiomatic: On arrival Chu Ai told his staff, 'Xun Xian will rise sky-high—treat him well.'

sentences.zh: 」尋遷建威將軍、吳國內史。

translations.literal: Soon transferred general who establishes might, interior minister of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he led Wu as general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 除北中郎將、徐州刺史、監徐兗二州揚州之晉陵諸軍事、假節。

translations.literal: Appointed general of the northern centre, inspector of Xuzhou—supervised Xu-Yan two prefectures and Yangzhou's Jinling military affairs—borrowed insignia.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Xu and Yan, Jinling sector of Yangzhou, as general of the northern centre with credentials.

sentences.zh: 殷浩以羨在事有能名，故居以重任。

translations.literal: Yin Hao because Xian in office had able name—therefore entrusted heavy duty.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Hao gave him the post because of his proven talent.

sentences.zh: 時年二十八，中興方伯，未有如羨之少者。

translations.literal: At the time age twenty-eight—restoration regional lords—none like Xian's youth.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-eight he was the youngest frontier commander of the restoration.

sentences.zh: 羨至鎮，發二州兵，使參軍鄭襲戍准陰。

translations.literal: Xian reached garrison—mobilized two prefectures' troops—ordered army adviser Zheng Xi garrison Huaiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He mobilized Xu and Yan and posted Zheng Xi at Huaiyin.

sentences.zh: 羨尋北鎮准陰，屯田于東陽之石鱉。

translations.literal: Xian soon north garrisoned Huaiyin—opened fields at Dongyang's Stone Turtle.
translations.idiomatic: He moved north to Huaiyin and opened military colonies at Stone Turtle in Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 尋加監青州諸軍事，又領兗州刺史，鎮下邳。

translations.idiomatic: That is my second fear.

translations.idiomatic: That is my third fear.

translations.literal: Shen-Bo beside frontier captains.
